title.zh: 卷19下 景穆十二王下
title.raw: 卷19下 景穆十二王下 Volume 19c: Emperor Jingmu Twelve Princes 3

sentences.zh: 任城王

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng

sentences.zh: 任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。

translations.literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was five years old when Gongzong died; he wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was only five when Gongzong died, yet he wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！

translations.literal: Shizu heard of it and summoned him, took him in his arms, and wept, saying: "How can you know enough to have the mind of a grown man!"
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard and called for him, took him in his arms, and wept. "How is it you already have a grown man's heart?"

sentences.zh: 」和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Heping he was enfeoffed and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and Grand General of Helong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year 5 he received his fief and was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and commander of Helong Garrison.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。

translations.literal: Under Xianzu he was made commander of all military affairs within and without the court and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, heard civil suits, and won great praise of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzu he commanded all armies at court and in the field, directed the Inner Palace at the Center, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。

translations.literal: In Yanxing, Xianzu gathered the ministers and wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanxing era Xianzu gathered his ministers, intending to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 王公卿士，莫敢先言。

translations.literal: Kings, dukes, and grandees dared speak first of none.
translations.idiomatic: Among kings, dukes, and grandees none dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。

translations.literal: Yun advanced and said: "Your Majesty is just now raising great peace and overseeing all within the seas—how could you go against the ancestral temples above and abandon the myriad people below?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun stepped forward. "Your Majesty is raising an age of peace and holds all under heaven—how could you turn your back on the ancestral temples and cast off the people?"

sentences.zh: 父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。

translations.literal: Father passing the throne to son has long been the way; since the rise of Imperial Wei there has been no change.
translations.idiomatic: Father passing rule to son is an ancient way; since Imperial Wei rose, that line has never been broken.

sentences.zh: 皇儲正統，聖德夙章。

translations.literal: The heir apparent holds the orthodox succession; sagely virtue was long manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince holds the orthodox succession; his sagely virtue was long plain to see.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，[1]輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to set aside dusty affairs and nourish the spirit in clarity and distance, the charge of the heir should continue the precious succession; if you wish to discard the heir,[1] lightly to shift the imperial seat—I fear that is not the former sages' intent and will startle men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly means to lay down worldly cares and dwell in clarity, the heir's charge should carry on the succession; but to discard the heir[1] and lightly move the throne—I fear that is not what the sages intended and will shock the realm.

sentences.zh: 又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。

translations.literal: Moreover, all under Heaven is the ancestral temples' all under Heaven, and Your Majesty would on a whim alter the sacred vessel—above you would offend the seven temples and seven spirits, below you would lengthen the road of treason and disorder; this is where fortune and misfortune arise. I beg deep thought and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestral temples, not to a whim that shifts the sacred vessel—offending the seven temples above and feeding rebellion below. Fortune and ruin turn on such a step. I beg Your Majesty to weigh it deeply.

sentences.zh: 」太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yuan He also advanced and said: "Your Majesty now wishes to choose among the outer princes and abdicate to the imperial uncle—I fear that in spring and autumn offerings the zhao and mu lines will fall into disorder, and that ten thousand generations hence there will surely be the reproach of inverted sacrifice. I deeply wish you to ponder the Prince of Rencheng's words."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan He added, "To choose an outer prince and abdicate to the imperial uncle will disorder the zhao and mu lines at the seasonal sacrifices and invite, ages hence, the reproach of inverted rites. I beg Your Majesty heed the Prince of Rencheng."

sentences.zh: 」東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。

translations.literal: Yuan Pi of Dongyang and others advanced and said: "The crown prince's sagely virtue was long manifest, yet in truth he is still very young."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Pi of Dongyang and others said, "The crown prince's virtue is plain, yet he is still a child."

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has only begun to survey state affairs; all under Heaven looks up in admiration, the whole realm inclines its heart. To exalt solitary goodness and not take the ten thousand things to heart—what of the ancestral temples, what of the hundred millions!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in your prime and has only begun to govern; the realm looks up to you. To seek private ease and ignore the ten thousand things—what becomes of the temples, what of the people?"

sentences.zh: 」顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。

translations.literal: Xianzu said: "The heir's palace is orthodox; he receives the end from Wenzu, and the lords assist him—what cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu said, "The heir holds the orthodox line, receives the mandate from Wenzu, and will have the lords' aid—what could be impossible?"

sentences.zh: 」於是傳位於高祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he abdicated to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。

translations.literal: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and followed Xianzu to campaign; they met on the Great Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier Yun was made Grand Commander of the Center Army, followed Xianzu to war, and met them on the Great Marsh.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The affair is given in full in the Rouran biography.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign is recorded in the Rouran biography.

sentences.zh: 後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。

translations.literal: Later the Di of Chouchi rebelled; Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chouchi Di rebelled he was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was removed and made commander of all military affairs along the Huai on Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, with an open office, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made commander of Huai-border armies in Xu and Yan, Grand General Who Conquers the East with an open office, and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲以太妃蓋氏薨，[2]表求解任，顯南安王 城陽王 章武王 樂陵王 安定王

translations.literal: When his grand consort Lady Gai died,[2] Yun memorialized asking to resign his post. Prince of Nan'an, Prince of Chengyang, Prince of Zhangwu, Prince of Leling, Prince of Anding
translations.idiomatic: When his grand consort Lady Gai died,[2] Yun asked to resign. What follows: the Princes of Nan'an, Chengyang, Zhangwu, Leling, and Anding

sentences.zh: 南安惠王楨

translations.literal: Zhen, Prince Hui of Nan'an
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Prince Hui of Nan'an

sentences.zh: 南安王楨，皇興二年封，加征南大將軍、中都大官，尋遷內都大官。

translations.literal: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing, appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon transferred to Director of the Inner Palace within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in Huangxing year 2, made Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon moved to the inner directorate.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，除涼州鎮都大將。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Grand General of Liangzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was made commander of Liangzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋以綏撫有能，加都督西戎諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護西域校尉、儀同三司、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, for able pacification, he was added commander of all military affairs of the Western Rong, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for skill in pacification, he was added commander of Western Rong armies, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵為內都大官，出為使持節、侍中、本將軍、開府、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Inner Palace within the capital, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, his former rank, with an open office, Grand General of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the inner directorate, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff and Palace Attendant with his former rank, an open office, command of Chang'an Garrison, and the Yongzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 楨性忠謹，事母以孝聞，賜帛千匹以褒之。

translations.literal: Zhen was by nature loyal and careful; he served his mother with a fame for filial piety and was rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was loyal and careful, famed for filial service to his mother; the court gave him a thousand bolts of silk in praise.

sentences.zh: 徵赴講武，高祖引見於皇信堂，戒之曰：「翁孝行著於私庭，令問彰於邦國，每欽忠懿，思一言展，故因講武，遠徵赴闕。

translations.literal: Summoned to the martial review, Gaozu received him in the Hall of Imperial Trust and admonished him: "Sir, your filial conduct is manifest in the private hall and your fair name shines in the state—each time I admire your loyal goodness I wish to speak with you at length; therefore at the martial review I summoned you from afar to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the martial review, Gaozu received him in the Hall of Imperial Trust and warned him: "Your filial conduct shines at home and your fair name in the realm; I have long wished to hear you speak, and so at the review I summoned you from afar.

sentences.zh: 仰戀仁慈，情在未已。

translations.literal: I look up in longing for your kindness; the feeling in my heart is not yet spent.
translations.idiomatic: I still yearn for your counsel; my heart is not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 但長安鎮年飢民儉，理須綏撫，不容久留，翁今還州，其勤隱恤，無令境內有飢餒之民。

translations.literal: But Chang'an Garrison has had famine these years and the people are straitened; it must be pacified and cannot long keep you here. Sir, return now to your province and work diligently to comfort and pity—let there be no hungry people within your borders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chang'an has known famine and the people are straitened; the post must be pacified and cannot keep you long. Return to your province, comfort the hidden poor, and let no one within your borders go hungry.

sentences.zh: 翁既國之懿親，終無貧賤之慮。

translations.literal: As a great kin of the state you will in the end have no worry of poverty.
translations.idiomatic: As a prince of the blood you need never fear want.

sentences.zh: 所宜慎者，略有三事：一者，恃親驕矜，違禮僭度；

translations.literal: What you should guard against are roughly three things: first, relying on kinship to be proud and arrogant, violating ritual and overstepping measure;
translations.idiomatic: What you must guard against are three things: first, pride of kinship that breaks ritual and oversteps bounds;

sentences.zh: 二者，傲慢貪奢，不恤政事；

translations.literal: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury without pity for government;
translations.idiomatic: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury without care for government;

sentences.zh: 三者，飲酒遊逸，不擇交友。

translations.literal: third, wine-drinking, roaming, and pleasure without choosing companions.
translations.idiomatic: third, wine, wandering, and careless company.

sentences.zh: 三者不去，患禍將生，但能慎此，足以全身遠害，光國榮家，終始之德成矣。

translations.literal: If these three are not cast off, misfortune will be born; if you can be careful in these, it is enough to preserve the body, keep harm far off, and bring glory to the state and honor to the house—the virtue of beginning and end will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not cast these off, ruin will follow; if you heed them, you may keep your person safe, harm at bay, and bring honor to throne and house from first to last."

sentences.zh: 」而楨不能遵奉，後乃聚斂肆情。

translations.literal: " Yet Zhen could not follow and obey; afterward he gathered wealth at will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen could not obey; afterward he amassed wealth as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 文明太后、高祖並臨皇信堂，引見王公，太后令曰：「汝陰王天賜、南安王楨不順法度，黷貨聚斂，依犯論坐，將至不測。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming and Gaozu both came to the Hall of Imperial Trust and received the kings and dukes; the empress dowager ordered: "The Prince of Ruyin, Tiansi, and the Prince of Nan'an, Zhen, do not follow the law; they profane goods and gather wealth. By the statutes they should be judged and sit in peril beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming and Gaozu received the princes in the Hall of Imperial Trust. The empress dowager said, "Prince Tiansi of Ruyin and Prince Zhen of Nan'an break the law, profane office, and hoard wealth. By statute they face death.

sentences.zh: 卿等為當存親以毀令，為欲滅親以明法？

translations.literal: Will you lords preserve kin and ruin the ordinance, or destroy kin to clarify the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you preserve kin and ruin the law, or destroy kin to make the law plain?"

sentences.zh: 」羣臣咸以二王託體先皇，宜蒙矜恕。

translations.literal: The ministers all said the two princes bore the former emperor's body and should receive compassion and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said both princes bore Gaozong's flesh and should be spared.

sentences.zh: 太后不答。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager did not reply.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃詔曰：「南安王楨以懿戚之貴，作鎮關右，不能潔己奉公，助宣皇度，方肆貪欲，殖貨私庭，放縱姦囚，壅絕訴訟，貨遺諸使，邀求虛稱，二三之狀，皆犯刑書。

translations.literal: Gaozu then issued an edict: "The Prince of Nan'an, Zhen, by the honor of close kin, held command west of the Pass; he could not cleanse himself and serve the public, help proclaim the imperial measure, but instead indulged greed, heaped goods in his private hall, released wicked prisoners, blocked suits at law, bribed envoys, and sought empty praise—two or three such counts all violate the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then decreed: "Prince Zhen of Nan'an, by grace of close kin, held the west of the Pass yet would not keep himself clean or aid the throne's measure; he indulged greed, stocked his private hall, freed wicked prisoners, blocked suits, bribed envoys, and sought empty praise—each count violates the penal code.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武翦髮以齊眾，叔向戮弟以明法，克己忍親，以率天下。

translations.literal: Formerly Cao Cao of Wei cut his hair to align the host; Shuqiu Xiang killed his younger brother to clarify the law—restraining oneself and bearing kin away to lead all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao of Wei once cut his hair to discipline the army; Shuqiu Xiang killed his brother to clarify the law—men who restrained themselves and bore kin away to lead the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不懷，有為而然耳。

translations.literal: Was it that they did not cherish them? They had business and acted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Did they not love them? They had a duty and acted.

sentences.zh: 今者所犯，事重疇日，循古推刑，實在難恕。

translations.literal: Today's offenses weigh heavier than yesterday's; following antiquity and pushing punishment, in truth they are hard to pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Today's crimes outweigh yesterday's; by ancient precedent punishment is hard to spare.

sentences.zh: 皇太后天慈寬篤，恩矜國屬，每一尋惟高宗孔懷之近，發言哽塞，悲慟于懷；

translations.literal: The empress dowager's heavenly kindness is broad and deep; in pity for the state's kin, each time she searches her thoughts on Gaozong's close embrace nearby, her words choke and grief fills her breast;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's kindness is deep; pitying the imperial kin, each time she thinks of Gaozong's close embrace her words choke and grief fills her;

sentences.zh: 且以南安王孝養之名，聞於內外；

translations.literal: and because the Prince of Nan'an's name for filial nurture is heard within and without;
translations.idiomatic: and because Prince Zhen of Nan'an is famed within and without for filial care;

sentences.zh: 特一原恕，削除封爵，以庶人歸第，禁錮終身。」

translations.literal: she has specially granted one pardon, struck off his enfeoffment, and sent him home as a commoner, confined for life."
translations.idiomatic: she has granted one pardon: his title is struck off, he returns home a commoner, and is confined for life."

sentences.zh: 後高祖南伐，楨從至洛，及議遷都，首從大計，高祖甚悅。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu campaigned south, Zhen followed to Luoyang; when the move of the capital was debated he was first to follow the great plan, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched south Zhen followed to Luoyang; at the debate over moving the capital he was first to endorse the great plan, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 楨母劉太妃薨，高祖親幸臨慰。

translations.literal: When Zhen's mother Grand Consort Liu died, Gaozu personally went to console him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Grand Consort Liu died, Gaozu went in person to console him.

sentences.zh: 及葬，贈布帛綵五百段。

translations.literal: At the burial he was given five hundred lengths of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial he was given five hundred lengths of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 又以楨議定遷都，復封南安王，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Again, because Zhen had settled the plan to move the capital, he was re-created Prince of Nan'an with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had helped settle the capital move, he was re-created Prince of Nan'an with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮北大將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand General Who Guards the North and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖餞楨於華林都亭。

translations.literal: Gaozu saw Zhen off at the Pavilion of the Imperial Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw him off at the Pavilion of the Imperial Grove.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「從祖南安，既之蕃任，將曠違千里，豫懷惘戀。

translations.literal: An edict said: "My paternal uncle of Nan'an, now going to his frontier post, will soon be a thousand li apart; I forefeel regret and longing.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "My paternal uncle of Nan'an goes to his frontier post; soon we shall be a thousand li apart, and I already feel regret.

sentences.zh: 然今者之集，雖曰分歧，實為曲宴，並可賦詩申意。

translations.literal: Yet today's gathering, though called a parting, is in truth a bent feast; all may compose poems to declare their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's gathering, though a farewell, is truly a feast bent to joy—all may compose poems to speak their hearts.

sentences.zh: 射者可以觀德，不能賦詩者，可聽射也。

translations.literal: Archery lets one view virtue; those who cannot compose poems may listen to the archery.
translations.idiomatic: Archery reveals virtue; those who cannot write may watch the bow.

sentences.zh: 當使武士彎弓，文人下筆。

translations.literal: Let warriors bend the bow and men of letters set brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: Let warriors bend the bow and scholars set brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 」高祖送楨於階下，流涕而別。

translations.literal: " Gaozu escorted Zhen down the steps and parted with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu walked him down the steps and parted in tears.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年五月至鄴，入治日，暴風大雨，凍死者十數人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taihe he reached Ye; on the day he entered administration a violent wind and great rain struck, and several tens froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 20, fifth month, he reached Ye; on his first day in office a violent wind and great rain struck, and several tens died of cold.

sentences.zh: 楨又以旱祈雨于羣神。

translations.literal: Zhen again prayed for rain to the host of spirits because of drought.
translations.idiomatic: During drought he again prayed for rain to the host of spirits.

sentences.zh: 鄴城有石虎廟，人奉祀之。

translations.literal: In Ye city there was a Stone Tiger shrine that the people worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had a Stone Tiger shrine that the people worshipped.

sentences.zh: 楨告虎神像云：「三日不雨，當加鞭罰。

translations.literal: Zhen addressed the Stone Tiger image and said: "If in three days there is no rain, I shall add the whip's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen addressed the Stone Tiger image: "If there is no rain in three days, I shall add the whip's punishment.

sentences.zh: 」請雨不驗，遂鞭像一百。

translations.literal: He prayed for rain without effect and then whipped the image a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer failed; he whipped the image a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 是月疽發背，薨。

translations.literal: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰惠，贈帛一千匹，及葬，又賜帛千匹，遣黃門郎監護喪事。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Hui; a thousand bolts of silk were given, and at the burial another thousand bolts, with a Yellow Gate Gentleman to oversee the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Prince Hui; a thousand bolts of silk were granted, and at burial another thousand, with a Yellow Gate Gentleman to oversee the rites.

sentences.zh: 及恒州刺史穆泰謀反，楨知而不告，雖薨，猶追奪爵封，國除。

translations.literal: When Hengzhou Inspector Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report; though already dead, his title was still posthumously stripped and the fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Hengzhou inspector Mu Tai rebelled, Zhen knew and did not report; though dead, his title was posthumously stripped and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 有五子。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons.

sentences.zh: 中山獻武王英

translations.literal: Ying, Prince Xianwu of Zhongshan
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Prince Xianwu of Zhongshan

sentences.zh: 子英，字虎兒。

translations.literal: His son Ying, styled Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying, courtesy name Hu'er.

sentences.zh: 性識聰敏，博聞強記，便弓馬，解吹笛，微曉醫術。

translations.literal: By nature he was clever and keen in perception, broadly learned with a strong memory, skilled at bow and horse, able to play the flute, and slightly versed in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and keen, broadly learned with a strong memory, he was skilled at bow and horse, could play the flute, and knew a little medicine.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，為平北將軍、武川鎮都大將、假魏公。

translations.literal: Under Gaozu he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Grand General of Wuchuan Garrison, and Acting Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was General Who Pacifies the North, commander of Wuchuan Garrison, and Acting Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷都督梁益寧三州諸軍事、安南將軍、領護西戎校尉、仇池鎮都大將、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to commander of all military affairs of Liang, Yi, and Ning, General Who Pacifies the South, Protector-General of the Western Rong, Grand General of Chouchi Garrison, and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of armies in Liang, Yi, and Ning, General Who Pacifies the South, Protector-General of the Western Rong, commander of Chouchi Garrison, and inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，為梁漢別道都將。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south he was commander of the separate route through Liang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozu's southern campaign he commanded the separate Liang-Han column.

sentences.zh: 後大駕臨鍾離，詔英率眾備寇境上。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage reached Zhongli, an edict ordered Ying to lead troops and guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Zhongli, an edict ordered Ying to guard the frontier with his troops.

sentences.zh: 英以大駕親動，勢傾東南，漢中有可乘之會，表求進討，高祖許之。

translations.literal: Ying, because the imperial carriage moved in person and momentum tilted toward the southeast, saw that Hanzhong offered an opening, memorialized asking to advance and attack, and Gaozu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor advance in person and momentum pour toward the southeast, Ying judged Hanzhong open, asked to strike, and Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 師次沮水，蕭鸞將蕭懿遣將尹紹祖、梁季羣等領眾二萬，徼山立柵，分為數處，居高視下，隔水為營。

translations.literal: The army halted at the Ju River; Xiao Luan's general Xiao Yi sent Yin Shaozu, Liang Jiqun, and others with twenty thousand men to take the mountains and raise palisades in several places, looking down from the heights and making camps across the water.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at the Ju River. Xiao Yi's general Xiao Yi sent Yin Shaozu and Liang Jiqun with twenty thousand men to seize the heights, raise palisades in several places, and camp across the water looking down.

sentences.zh: 英乃謀曰：「彼帥賤民慢，莫能相服，眾而無上，罔知適從。

translations.literal: Ying then counseled: "Their commanders despise the people and are arrogant; none can make the rest obey. Many men without a head—they do not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ying counseled, "Their leaders despise the men and cannot command them. A host without a head does not know whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 若選精卒，并攻一營，彼不相救，我克必矣。

translations.literal: If we choose crack troops and together strike one camp, they will not rescue one another and we are sure to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Choose crack troops and strike one camp together—they will not aid one another and we are sure to win.

sentences.zh: 若克一軍，四營自拔。

translations.literal: If we take one army, the four camps will pull themselves up of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Break one camp and the other four will collapse of themselves."

sentences.zh: 」於是簡兵三面騰上，果不相救。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he picked troops and charged up on three sides; indeed they did not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: He picked troops and charged on three sides; as he foresaw, they did not aid one another.

sentences.zh: 既破一處，四營俱潰，生擒梁季羣，斬三千餘級，俘七百人。

translations.literal: Once one place was broken, all four camps collapsed; Liang Jiqun was taken alive, more than three thousand were beheaded, and seven hundred captured.
translations.idiomatic: One position fell and all four camps broke; Liang Jiqun was taken alive, more than three thousand beheaded, seven hundred captured.

sentences.zh: 鸞白馬戍將其夜逃潰。

translations.literal: Luan's White Horse Garrison general fled in the night and dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's garrison at White Horse fled in the night and dissolved.

sentences.zh: 乘勝長驅，將逼南鄭，漢川之民，以為神也，相率歸附。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in a long drive, he was about to close on Nanzheng; the people of Hanzhong took him for a god and came in succession to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory he drove toward Nanzheng; the people of Hanzhong took him for a god and submitted in waves.

sentences.zh: 梁州民李天幹等詣英降，待以國士之禮。

translations.literal: Liangzhou man Li Tian'gan and others came to Ying to surrender and were treated with the rites due a champion of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tian'gan of Liangzhou and others surrendered to Ying and were treated as champions of the state.

sentences.zh: 天幹等家在南鄭之西，請師迎接，英遣迎之。

translations.literal: Tian'gan and the rest had families west of Nanzheng and asked troops to welcome them; Ying sent men to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'gan's kin lay west of Nanzheng; he asked for troops to fetch them, and Ying sent escorts.

sentences.zh: 蕭懿聞而遣將姜脩率眾追襲，逮夜交戰，頗有殺傷。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi heard and sent General Jiang Xiu with troops to pursue and strike; at night they fought and there were considerable casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi heard and sent Jiang Xiu in pursuit; they fought at night with heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 脩後屢敗，復更請軍。

translations.literal: Xiu afterward was repeatedly defeated and again asked for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was beaten again and again and asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 懿遣眾赴之，迎者告急。

translations.literal: Yi sent troops to go; the welcomers reported urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent reinforcements; the escort party cried urgent need.

sentences.zh: 英率騎一千，倍道赴救。

translations.literal: Ying led a thousand horse and went by double marches to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Ying led a thousand horse at double march to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 未至，賊已退還。

translations.literal: Before he arrived the bandits had already retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived the enemy had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 英恐其入城，別遣統軍元拔以隨其後，英徼其前，合擊之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Ying feared they would enter the city; he separately sent the commandery general Yuan Ba to follow behind them while Ying intercepted before them and struck together, capturing the whole host.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would enter the city, he sent Commandery General Yuan Ba to follow behind while he himself blocked the front; together they took the whole force.

sentences.zh: 懿續遣軍，英不虞賊至，且眾力已疲，軍少人懼，咸欲奔走。

translations.literal: Yi continued to send troops; Ying did not expect the bandits to arrive, and as his force was already weary and few, the men were afraid and all wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent more troops; Ying did not expect them, his men were weary and few, and all wished to run.

sentences.zh: 英乃緩騎徐行，神色自若，登高望賊，東西指麾，狀似處分，然後整列而前。

translations.literal: Ying then slowed his horse and advanced at ease, his expression calm; he climbed high to view the bandits, pointing and commanding east and west as if disposing troops, then arrayed the ranks and went forward.
translations.idiomatic: Ying slowed his horse, face calm, climbed high to view the enemy, gestured east and west as if disposing troops, then re-formed ranks and advanced.

sentences.zh: 賊謂有伏兵。

translations.literal: The bandits thought there were ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy thought ambush lay in wait.

sentences.zh: 俄然賊退，乘勢追殄，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: Soon the bandits retreated; pressing the momentum he pursued and destroyed them, then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they withdrew; he pursued, destroyed them, and besieged Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 禁止三軍，一無所犯，遠近皆供租運。

translations.literal: He forbade the three armies from a single violation; near and far all supplied grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his three armies every violation; near and far the people brought grain.

sentences.zh: 先是，英未至也，蕭懿遣軍主范潔領三千餘人伐獠。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Ying had arrived, Xiao Yi had sent the army commander Fan Jie with more than three thousand men to attack the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ying arrived, Xiao Yi had sent Army Commander Fan Jie with more than three thousand men against the Liao.

sentences.zh: 潔聞大軍圍城，欲還救援。

translations.literal: Jie heard the great army besieged the city and wished to return to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Jie heard the great army had besieged the city and turned back to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 英遣統軍李平敵、李鐵騎等收合巴西、晉壽土人，以斷其路。

translations.literal: Ying sent the commandery generals Li Pingdi and Li Tieqi and others to gather the men of Baxi and Jinshou and cut his road.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent Li Pingdi, Li Tieqi, and others to rally men of Baxi and Jinshou and cut Jie's road.

sentences.zh: 潔以死決戰，遂敗平敵之軍。

translations.literal: Jie fought to the death and thereupon defeated Pingdi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jie fought to the death and broke Pingdi's force.

sentences.zh: 英候其稍近，以奇兵掩之，盡皆擒獲。

translations.literal: Ying waited until they drew somewhat near, then with odd troops masked them and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ying waited until they drew near, then ambushed and took them all.

sentences.zh: 攻圍九十餘日，戰無不克。

translations.literal: The siege lasted more than ninety days; in battle nothing failed.
translations.idiomatic: The siege ran more than ninety days; every assault succeeded.

sentences.zh: 被敕班師。

translations.literal: He received orders to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Orders came to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 英於是先遣老弱，身勒精卒留後，遣使與懿告別。

translations.literal: Ying thereupon first sent off the old and weak, himself led crack troops to remain behind, and sent a messenger to take leave of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying first sent off the old and weak, kept crack troops in the rear himself, and sent a messenger to bid Yi farewell.

sentences.zh: 懿以為詐也，英還一日，猶閉門不開。

translations.literal: Yi thought it a trick; one day after Ying had gone he still did not open the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yi thought it a ruse; a full day after Ying left the gates stayed shut.

sentences.zh: 二日之後，懿乃遣將追英。

translations.literal: Two days afterward Yi then sent a general to pursue Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Yi sent a general in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 英親自殿後，與士卒下馬交戰，賊眾莫敢逼之。

translations.literal: Ying himself brought up the rear and dismounted with the soldiers to fight hand to hand; the bandit host dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying brought up the rear himself, fought dismounted with his men, and the enemy dared not press close.

sentences.zh: 四日四夜，然後賊退，全軍而還。

translations.literal: Four days and four nights, and then the bandits withdrew; the whole army returned intact.
translations.idiomatic: For four days and four nights the enemy hung back; then they withdrew and the whole army returned intact.

sentences.zh: 會山氐並反，斷英歸路。

translations.literal: Just then the mountain Di all rebelled and cut Ying's road of return.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the mountain Di rebelled and cut his road home.

sentences.zh: 英勒眾奮擊，且戰且行，為流矢所中，軍人莫有知者。

translations.literal: Ying drove the host in fierce attack, fighting as he marched; he was struck by a stray arrow, and the soldiers did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: He drove his men in fierce attack, fighting as he marched; a stray arrow struck him, and none knew.

sentences.zh: 以功遷安南大將軍，賜爵廣武伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and granted the rank Baron of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Baron of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 在仇池六載，甚有威惠之稱。

translations.literal: Six years at Chouchi; he had a great name for authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Six years at Chouchi won him a great name for stern kindness.

sentences.zh: 父憂，解任。

translations.literal: His father's mourning; he resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death he resigned.

sentences.zh: 後英還京師，上表曰：「臣聞取亂悔亡，有國之常道；

translations.literal: Later Ying returned to the capital and submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that taking disorder and repenting ruin is a state's constant way;
translations.idiomatic: Later, back in the capital, he memorialized: "I have heard that seizing disorder and repenting ruin is a state's constant way;

sentences.zh: 陳師鞠旅，因機而致發。

translations.literal: arraying troops and mustering hosts is to strike as opportunity offers.
translations.idiomatic: arraying troops is to strike when opportunity offers.

sentences.zh: 竊以區區寶卷，罔顧天常，憑恃山河，敢抗中國。

translations.literal: I venture to think that petty Baojuan, heedless of heaven's constant, relies on mountains and rivers and dares resist the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: I venture that petty Baojuan, heedless of heaven's law, trusts his mountains and rivers and dares resist the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 今妖逆數亡，驕縱日甚，威侮五行，怠棄三正，淫刑以逞，虐害無辜。

translations.literal: Now the demon rebels are several times destroyed, arrogance and license grow daily, he insults the Five Agents, neglects the Three Alignments, uses cruel punishments to his heart's content, and harms the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: His rebels are several times broken, yet arrogance grows daily; he insults the Five Agents, neglects the calendar, tortures at will, and harms the innocent.

sentences.zh: 其雍州刺史蕭衍東伐秣陵，掃土興兵，順流而下，唯有孤城，更無重衞。

translations.literal: His Inspector of Yongzhou, Xiao Yan, eastward attacks Moling, sweeps the land and raises troops, flows down the river—and there is only a lone city, no second guard.
translations.idiomatic: His Yongzhou inspector Xiao Yan attacks Moling eastward, sweeps the land, raises troops, and drifts downriver—leaving only a lone city without a second guard.

sentences.zh: 此則皇天授我之日，曠載一逢之秋，事易走丸，理同拾芥，此而不乘，將欲何待。

translations.literal: This is the day heaven grants us, the autumn met once in vast ages; the affair is easy as rolling a pellet, the principle like picking up a mustard seed—if we do not ride this, what shall we wait for?
translations.idiomatic: This is the day heaven grants us, an autumn that comes once in vast ages; the task is easy as rolling a pellet, simple as plucking a mustard seed—if we do not ride this moment, what shall we wait for?

sentences.zh: 臣乞躬率步騎三萬，直指沔陰，據襄陽之城，斷黑水之路。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to lead thirty thousand foot and horse in person straight to the Mian's north, hold the city of Xiangyang, and cut the Black Water road.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to lead thirty thousand foot and horse straight to the north bank of the Mian, hold Xiangyang, and cut the Black Water road.

sentences.zh: 昏虐君臣，自相魚肉。

translations.literal: The benighted and cruel ruler and ministers will devour one another like fish.
translations.idiomatic: Their benighted ruler and ministers will devour one another like fish.

sentences.zh: 我居上流，威震遐邇，長驅南出，進拔江陵。

translations.literal: We hold the upper stream, our authority shaking far and near; a long drive southward will advance to take Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the upper stream we shake the far reaches; a long drive south will seize Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 其路既近，不盈五百，則三楚之地，一朝可收，岷蜀之道，自成斷絕。

translations.literal: The road is near, not five hundred li; then the land of the Three Chu may be gathered in one morning, and the road to Min and Shu will of itself be cut.
translations.idiomatic: The road is near—less than five hundred li—then the Three Chu may fall in a morning and the road to Min and Shu will cut itself off.

sentences.zh: 又命揚徐二州，聲言俱舉，緣江焚毀，靡使所遺。

translations.literal: Also order Yang and Xu provinces to proclaim that both will rise together, burn along the river, and leave nothing behind.
translations.idiomatic: Order Yang and Xu to proclaim a joint rising, burn along the river, and leave nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 建業窮蹙，魚遊釜內。

translations.literal: Jianye will be cornered, a fish in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye will be cornered—a fish in the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 士治之師再興，孫皓之縛重至，齊文軌而大同，混天地而為一。

translations.literal: The army of a well-governed state will rise again, Sun Hao's bonds will come once more, the text and wheel will be made one, heaven and earth mixed into one.
translations.idiomatic: The army of a well-governed state will rise again, Sun Hao's bonds will return, the text and wheel will be one, heaven and earth merged.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下暫闢旒纊，少垂聽覽，獨決聖心，無取疑議，此期脫爽，并吞未日。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty will for a time set aside the imperial capstrings, slightly incline your ear, decide in your sage heart alone without taking doubtful counsel—if this term slips away, the day of swallowing whole is not yet come.
translations.idiomatic: I bow and beg Your Majesty to set aside the capstrings awhile, incline your ear, decide in your sage heart without doubtful counsel—if this season slips away, the day of swallowing whole is not yet here."

sentences.zh: 」事寢不報。

translations.literal: The affair was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 英又奏曰：「臣聞乘虛討弱，事在速舉，因危攻昧，徼捷可期。

translations.literal: Ying again memorialized: "Your servant has heard that striking the weak by void, the affair lies in swift raising; attacking the obscure by peril, sudden merit may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized again: "I hear that striking weakness through void lies in swift action; attacking peril through obscurity promises sudden merit.

sentences.zh: 今寶卷亂常，骨肉相賊，蕃戍鼎立，莫知所歸。

translations.literal: Now Baojuan disorders the constant; bone and flesh harm one another; frontier garrisons stand like tripods and none knows where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Now Baojuan disorders the constant; kin turn on kin; frontier garrisons stand like tripods and none knows where to turn.

sentences.zh: 義陽孤絕，密邇天境，外靡糧援之期，內無兵儲之固。

translations.literal: Yiyang stands isolated, close to our heavenly border; without grain support from outside, within it has no store of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang stands alone, close to our border; without grain from outside, within it has no arms store.

sentences.zh: 此乃臨焚之鳥，不可去薪；

translations.literal: This is a bird facing the blaze—one cannot remove the fuel;
translations.idiomatic: This is a bird facing the blaze—you cannot remove the fuel;

sentences.zh: 授首之寇，何容緩斧。

translations.literal: a foe offering his head—how can the axe be slow?
translations.idiomatic: a foe offering his head—how can the axe be slow?

sentences.zh: 若此行有果，則江右之地，斯為經略之基；

translations.literal: If this march has fruit, then the lands right of the river will be the base of further planning;
translations.idiomatic: If this march succeeds, the lands south of the river become the base of further planning;

sentences.zh: 如脫否也，非直後舉難圖，亦或居安生疾。

translations.literal: if it misses, not only will later efforts be hard to plot, but perhaps even in peace sickness will grow.
translations.idiomatic: if it fails, later efforts grow hard—and even in peace sickness may grow.

sentences.zh: [1]今豫州刺史司馬悅已戒嚴垂邁，而東豫州刺史田益宗方擬守三關，請遣軍司為之節度。

translations.literal: [1]Now Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Yue has already ordered alert and is about to march, while Inspector of East Yuzhou Tian Yizong is just planning to hold the Three Passes—please send a army supervisor to command them.
translations.idiomatic: [1]Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Yue has already ordered alert and is about to march, while East Yuzhou inspector Tian Yizong plans to hold the Three Passes—please send an army supervisor to command them.

sentences.zh: 」世宗遣直寢羊靈引為軍司。

translations.literal: " Shizong sent the Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 以軍功拜吏部尚書，以前後軍功進爵常山侯。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing; for successive military achievements he was advanced to Marquis of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing; for further victories he was advanced to Marquis of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 英奏：「謹案學令：諸州郡學生，三年一校所通經數，因正使列之，然後遣使就郡練考。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized: "According to the school ordinance: students of the various provinces and commanderies are once every three years examined on the classics they have mastered, listed by the regular envoy, and then an envoy is sent to the commandery to drill and examine.
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized: "According to the school ordinance, provincial students are every three years examined on classics mastered, listed by the regular envoy, then an envoy drills and examines in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣伏惟聖明，崇道顯成均之風，蘊義光膠序之美，是以太學之館久置於下國，四門之教方構於京瀍。

translations.literal: Your servant bows and considers the sage brightness, exalting the Way and displaying the wind of the accomplished academy, storing righteousness and shining the beauty of the glue-and-lacquer sequence—therefore the Grand Academy's halls were long set in the lower states, and the Four Gates' teaching was just then built at the capital ford.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before sage brightness that exalts the Way, displays the academy's wind, stores righteousness, and shines the glue-and-lacquer schools—therefore the Grand Academy stood long in the provinces and the Four Gates were just raised at the capital ford.

sentences.zh: 計習訓淹年，聽受累紀，然儁造之流應問於魏闕，不革之輩宜返於齊民，使就郡練考，覈其最殿。

translations.literal: I reckon that training and study run over years, hearing and receiving may span many cycles, yet the outstanding stream should be questioned at the Wei gate, and the unaltered remainder should return to the common folk—let them undergo commandery drill and examination and verify the highest and lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Training runs years, study many cycles—yet the outstanding should be questioned at the Wei gate and the unfit returned to the people, examined in the commanderies and ranked highest to lowest.

sentences.zh: 頃以皇都遷構，江揚未一，故鄉校之訓，弗遑正試。

translations.literal: Recently, because the imperial capital was moved and Jiang and Yang were not yet one, the commandery schools' instruction could not attend to the regular trial.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, with the capital moved and Jiang and Yang not yet one, commandery schools could not hold the regular trial.

sentences.zh: 致使薰蕕之質，均誨學庭；

translations.literal: It has caused the quality of wormwood and artemisia to be equally taught in the school court;
translations.idiomatic: Wormwood and artemisia alike sit in the school court;

sentences.zh: 蘭蕭之體，等教文肆。

translations.literal: orchid and mugwort alike receive instruction in the literary stalls.
translations.idiomatic: orchid and mugwort alike are taught in the literary stalls.

sentences.zh: 今外宰京官，銓考向訖，求遣四門博士明通五經者，道別校練，依令黜陟。

translations.literal: Now the outer prefects and capital officials have finished their review appointments; I ask to send Four Gates academicians clear in the Five Classics to examine separately by the Way and, according to the ordinance, promote and demote.
translations.idiomatic: Outer prefects and capital officials have finished review; I ask to send Four Gates doctors versed in the Five Classics to examine by the Way and promote or demote by ordinance.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「學業墮廢，為日已久，非一使能勸，比當別敕。」

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Scholarly work has long lain in ruin—not one envoy can urge it; presently there will be a separate decree."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, "Scholarly work has lain in ruin for long—not one envoy can restore it; a separate decree will follow."

sentences.zh: 尋詔英使持節、假鎮南將軍、都督征義陽諸軍事，率眾南討。

translations.literal: Soon an edict made Ying Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of all armies campaigning on Yiyang, leading troops south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, commander of armies on Yiyang, and led troops south.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍司州刺史蔡道恭聞英將至，遣其驍騎將軍楊由率城外居民三千餘家，於城西南十里賢首山即嶺為三柵，作表裏之勢。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Sizhou, Cai Daogong, heard Ying was coming and sent his fierce-cavalry general Yang You to lead more than three thousand households of residents outside the city to Xianshou Mountain ten li southwest of the city, taking the ridge to make three palisades in an inner-outer disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Sizhou inspector Cai Daogong heard Ying was coming and sent Fierce-Cavalry General Yang You with more than three thousand households from outside the city to Xianshou Mountain ten li southwest, where they took the ridge for three palisades in inner-outer array.

sentences.zh: 英勒諸軍圍賢首壘，焚其柵門。

translations.literal: Ying drove the armies to besiege the Xianshou stronghold and burned the palisade gates.
translations.idiomatic: Ying besieged the Xianshou stronghold and burned the palisade gates.

sentences.zh: 楊由乃驅水牛，從營而出，繼之以兵。

translations.literal: Yang You then drove water buffalo out of the camp, with troops following.
translations.idiomatic: Yang You drove water buffalo from the camp with troops behind.

sentences.zh: 軍人避牛，師遂退下。

translations.literal: The soldiers avoided the buffalo and the army thereupon withdrew downhill.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers dodged the buffalo and the army fell back downhill.

sentences.zh: 尋分兵圍守。

translations.literal: Soon he divided troops to surround and hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he divided troops to surround and hold them.

sentences.zh: 其夜，柵民任馬駒斬由以降。

translations.literal: That night the palisade man Ren Maju beheaded You and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the palisade man Ren Maju beheaded You and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三軍館穀，降民安堵。

translations.literal: The three armies were quartered on grain; the surrendered people were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies fed on captured grain; the surrendered people were settled in peace.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其平西將軍曹景宗、後將軍王僧炳等率步騎三萬來救義陽。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Pacifies the West, Cao Jingzong, and Rear General Wang Sengbing and others with thirty thousand foot and horse to rescue Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent General Who Pacifies the West Cao Jingzong and Rear General Wang Sengbing with thirty thousand foot and horse to rescue Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 僧炳統眾二萬據鑿峴，景宗率一萬繼後。

translations.literal: Sengbing commanded twenty thousand and held Zao Pass; Jingzong led ten thousand and followed after.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbing held Zao Pass with twenty thousand; Jingzong followed with ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 英遣冠軍將軍元逞、揚烈將軍曹文敬進據樊城以抗之。

translations.literal: Ying sent the Champion General Yuan Cheng and the Yanglie General Cao Wenjing forward to hold Fancheng against them.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent Champion General Yuan Cheng and Yanglie General Cao Wenjing to hold Fancheng against them.

sentences.zh: 英部勒將士，掎角討之，大破僧炳軍，俘斬四千餘人。

translations.literal: Ying arrayed his officers and men, attacked from corner to corner, and greatly defeated Sengbing's army, capturing and beheading more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ying arrayed his men, attacked corner to corner, and broke Sengbing's army, capturing or killing more than four thousand.

sentences.zh: 英又於士雅山結壘，與景宗相抗，分遣諸統，伏於四山，示之以弱。

translations.literal: Ying again built a stronghold on Shiya Mountain to oppose Jingzong, separately sending the various commanders to lie in ambush on the four mountains and show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: He built a camp on Shiya Mountain against Jingzong, sent commanders to ambush on four mountains, and feigned weakness.

sentences.zh: 衍將馬仙琕率眾萬餘，來掩英營。

translations.literal: Yan's general Ma Xianzun led more than ten thousand men to mask Ying's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's general Ma Xianzun led more than ten thousand to strike Ying's camp.

sentences.zh: 英命諸軍偽北誘之，既至平地，統軍傅永等三軍擊之，賊便奔退。

translations.literal: Ying ordered the armies to feign a northward retreat to lure them; once they reached level ground, Commandery General Fu Yong and three armies struck them and the bandits at once fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying feigned retreat north to lure them; on level ground Commandery General Fu Yong and three armies struck and the enemy fled at once.

sentences.zh: 進擊潰之，斬首二千三百級，斬賊羽林監軍鄧終年。

translations.literal: Pressing the attack he routed them, beheading more than two thousand three hundred, and beheading the bandits' Forest Guard supervisor Deng Zhongnian.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the attack he routed them, beheading more than two thousand three hundred and killing the enemy Forest Guard supervisor Deng Zhongnian.

sentences.zh: 仙琕又率一萬餘人，重來決戰。

translations.literal: Xianbi again led more than ten thousand men and came again for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xianbi rallied another ten thousand men and returned for a final clash.

sentences.zh: 英勒諸將，隨便分擊，又破之，復斬賊將陳秀之。

translations.literal: Ying urged the generals and, as opportunity allowed, divided to strike; he broke them again and again beheaded the rebel general Chen Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying drove his commanders to strike wherever chance offered, routed them once more, and beheaded the Liang general Chen Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 統軍王買奴別破東嶺之陣，斬首五百。

translations.literal: Army commander Wang Mainu separately broke the formation at East Ridge and took five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Wang Mainu broke the East Ridge line on his own and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 道恭憂死，驍騎將軍、行州事蔡靈恩復憑窮城，短兵日接。

translations.literal: Dao Gong died of worry; Valiant Cavalry General and acting provincial governor Cai Ling'en again relied on the desperate city, close combat joining day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gong died of grief; Cai Ling'en, Valiant Cavalry General acting as governor, still held the doomed city as hand-to-hand fighting met day after day.

sentences.zh: 景宗、仙琕知城將拔，盡銳決戰，一日三交，皆大敗而返。

translations.literal: Jingzong and Xianbi, knowing the city would soon fall, brought their full strength to decisive battle—three clashes in one day—and all were utterly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and Xianbi, seeing the city was lost, threw in every man for three battles in a single day—and were routed each time.

sentences.zh: 靈恩勢窘，遂降。

translations.literal: Ling'en's position was desperate and he thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Ling'en surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三關戍聞之，亦棄城而走。

translations.literal: The garrisons of the Three Passes, hearing of it, also abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news, the Three Passes garrisons abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「知賊城已下，復克三關，展威闢境，聲略宣振，公私稱泰，良以欣然。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Knowing the rebel city has fallen and the Three Passes have again been taken, extending might and opening the borders, fame and strategy proclaimed and shaken, public and private all declare peace—truly I am well pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wrote: "The rebel stronghold is down and the Three Passes retaken—might spread across the frontier, your name and plan ringing far; court and country rejoice, and so do I.

sentences.zh: 將軍淵規內斷，忠謨外舉，受律揚旌，克申廟算，雖方叔之制蠻荊，邵虎之掃淮浦，匹茲蔑如也。

translations.literal: The general's deep counsel within, loyal designs raised without, receiving the statutes and raising the banners, fulfilling the temple's plan—though Fang Shu's subduing of the Man and Jing, or Shao Hu's sweeping of the Huai shore, compared with this they are as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: You read the enemy within and laid loyal plans without; under law you raised the standard and fulfilled what the ancestors had plotted. Fang Shu taming the south, Shao Hu clearing the Huai—beside this they are nothing.

sentences.zh: 新州初附，宜廣經略，想善加檢督，必令周固，有所委付，然後凱旋耳。

translations.literal: Xin Province has newly submitted; you should broadly extend strategy. I trust you will well oversee and inspect, surely making it secure all round; when you have entrusted matters, then return in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou has only just submitted—extend your strategy there, oversee it well until all is secure, entrust what must be entrusted, and then march home in triumph."

sentences.zh: 」初，高祖之平漢陽，英有戰功，許復其封，反為顯達所敗，遂寢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu pacified Hanyang, Ying had merit in battle; restoration of his fief was promised, but in the end he was defeated by Xianda and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu pacified Hanyang, Ying had earned merit and a promise to restore his fief—but Xianda defeated him and the grant was shelved.

sentences.zh: 是役也，世宗大悅，乃復之，改封中山王，食邑一千戶，遣大使、鴻臚少卿睦延吉持節就拜。

translations.literal: In this campaign Emperor Shizong was greatly pleased and restored it; his fief was changed to Prince of Zhongshan with a household of one thousand, and Grand Envoy, Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations Mu Yanji was sent with credentials to invest him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: This time Shizong was delighted: the fief was restored as Prince of Zhongshan, one thousand households, and Grand Envoy Mu Yanji of the Court for Diplomatic Relations came with credentials to invest him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 英送蔡靈恩及衍尚書郎蔡僧勰、前軍將軍、義陽太守馮道要，游擊將軍鮑懷慎，天門太守王承伯，平北府司馬宗象，平北府諮議參軍伏粲，給事中、寧朔將軍蔡道基，中兵參軍龐脩等數十人。

translations.literal: Ying sent up Cai Ling'en together with Yan's Masters of Writing Attendant Cai Sengrui, Forward Army General and Yiyang Governor Feng Daoyao, Mobile Army General Bao Huaixin, Tianmen Governor Wang Chengbo, Pacify-the-North Staff Major Zong Xiang, Pacify-the-North Staff Adviser Fu Can, Palace Attendant and Pacify-the-North General Cai Daoji, Central Army Major Pang Xiu, and several tens more.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent up Cai Ling'en and dozens more—among them Yan's attendant Cai Sengrui, Feng Daoyao of Yiyang, Bao Huaixin, Wang Chengbo, Zong Xiang, Fu Can, Cai Daoji, and Pang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「會平江南，此等便可放歸也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When we pacify the south of the Yangzi, these may all be released to return.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "When the lands south of the Yangzi are pacified, release them all to go home."

sentences.zh: 」英既還，世宗引見，深嘉勞之，後增封一千戶。

translations.literal: When Ying had returned, Shizong received him in audience, deeply praised and comforted him, and later added one thousand households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying returned, Shizong received him, praised him at length, and later added another thousand households.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將軍寇肥梁，詔英使持節，加散騎常侍、征南將軍、都督揚徐二道諸軍事，率眾十萬討之，所在皆以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent generals to raid Fei Liang; an edict made Ying bearer of the staff, added Scattered Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Pacifies the South, and Area Commander of military affairs on the Yang and Xu routes, with a host of one hundred thousand to suppress them, acting at discretion wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent troops against Fei Liang; Ying was given the staff, made scattered-cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of Yang and Xu with a hundred thousand men, free to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 詔英曰：「賊勢滋甚，圍逼肥梁，邊將後規，以至於此。

translations.literal: An edict to Ying said: "The rebels' power grows daily; they press Fei Liang, and border generals lagged in planning until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told Ying: "The enemy grows stronger by the day and presses Fei Liang; frontier commanders dawdled until we reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 故有斯舉，必期勝捷，而出軍淹滯，肥梁已陷。

translations.literal: Therefore this move was made, surely expecting victory—but the army went out and stalled, and Fei Liang has fallen.
translations.idiomatic: We sent you expecting sure victory—yet the host stalled, and Fei Liang is lost.

sentences.zh: 聞之惋懣，實乖本圖。

translations.literal: Hearing it, I am aggrieved and troubled; truly it betrays the original plan.
translations.idiomatic: The news wounds me; it is far from what we intended.

sentences.zh: 今眾軍雲集，十有五萬，進取之方，其算安在？

translations.literal: Now the armies gather—one hundred fifty thousand in all. What is your plan for the advance?
translations.idiomatic: Now a hundred fifty thousand stand ready. What is your plan of attack?

sentences.zh: 克殄之期，復當遠近？

translations.literal: When may we expect their destruction—near or far?
translations.idiomatic: How soon will they be destroyed—weeks or months?

sentences.zh: 竟以幾日可至賊？

translations.literal: In how many days may we reach the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: How many days until you meet the enemy?

sentences.zh: 所必勝之規，何者為先？

translations.literal: Among the measures sure to win, which comes first?
translations.idiomatic: Of the moves that must win, which comes first?

sentences.zh: 故遣步兵校尉、領中書舍人王雲指取機要。

translations.literal: Therefore Infantry Commandant and Acting Director of Palace Secretariat Wang Yun is sent to take your key plans.
translations.idiomatic: I send Infantry Commandant Wang Yun of the Secretariat to hear your plans."

sentences.zh: 」英表陳事機。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized stating the opportunities.
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized on the situation.

sentences.zh: 乃擊破陰陵，斬衍將二十五人及虜首五千餘級。

translations.literal: He then broke Yinling and beheaded twenty-five of Yan's generals and more than five thousand heads of captives.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Yinling, beheaded twenty-five of Yan's generals, and took more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又頻破賊軍於梁城，斬其支將四十二人，殺獲及溺死者將五萬。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly broke the rebel armies at Liangcheng, beheading forty-two of their sub-generals; killed, captured, and drowned totaled nearly fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he broke Yan's armies at Liangcheng, killed forty-two subordinate commanders, and left nearly fifty thousand dead, captured, or drowned.

sentences.zh: 衍中軍大將軍、臨川王蕭宏，尚書右僕射柳惔等大將五人沿淮南走，[2]凡收米三十萬石。

translations.literal: Yan's Central Army Grand General, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yan, and five other great generals fled along the Huai south;[2] in all thirty myriads of grain were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Central Army Grand General Xiao Hong of Linchuan, Right Vice Director Liu Yan, and five other great commanders fled south along the Huai;[2] thirty myriads of grain were seized.

sentences.zh: 詔勞英曰：「知大摧鯨寇，威振南海，江浦無塵，三楚卷壒，聲被荒隅，同軌斯始，公私慶慰，良副朕懷。

translations.literal: An edict comforted Ying: "Knowing you have greatly shattered the whale-like rebels, might shaken across the southern sea, the river shores without dust, the Three Chu rolled in dust, fame reaching the wild corners, the same track beginning—public and private rejoice and comfort; truly it matches my heart.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him: "You have shattered the great foe, your might shaking the southern sea; the river shores are clean, the Three Chu lie in dust, your fame reaches the wild marches, and the realm begins to walk one path—court and country rejoice, as I do.

sentences.zh: 便當乘威藉響，長驅吳會，翦拉遺燼，截彼東南也。」

translations.literal: You should ride the momentum and sound, long-drive to Wu and Kuai, cut and pull the remaining embers, and sever their southeast."
translations.idiomatic: Ride that momentum long into Wu and Kuai, cut the last embers, and break their hold on the southeast."

sentences.zh: 英追至于馬頭，衍馬頭戍主委城遁走，遂圍鍾離。

translations.literal: Ying pursued to Matou; Yan's Matou garrison commander abandoned the city and fled, and he thereupon besieged Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pursued to Matou; Yan's garrison commander fled, and he besieged Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「師行已久，士馬疲瘠，賊城險固，卒難攻屠。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The army has marched long; men and horses are worn and lean; the rebel city is perilous and firm—sudden storming is hard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The campaign has run long; men and horses are spent; the city is steep and hard to storm.

sentences.zh: 冬春之交，稍非勝便，十萬之眾，日費無貲。

translations.literal: Between winter and spring it is slightly not the time of advantage; a host of one hundred thousand spends daily without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Winter turning to spring is no season for victory; a hundred thousand mouths cost a fortune each day.

sentences.zh: 方圖後舉，不待今事。

translations.literal: We are plotting a later move—do not wait on this affair.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to strike later—do not hang everything on this siege.

sentences.zh: 且可密裝徐嚴，為振旅之意，整疆完土，開示威略。

translations.literal: For now you may secretly prepare the Xu defenses as if for a triumphal return, secure the borders and complete the soil, and open display of might and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly ready the Xu line as if for withdrawal, secure the borders, and show your strategy.

sentences.zh: 左右蠻楚，素應逃亡，或竄山湖，或難制掠。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Chu left and right have always been prone to flight; some hide in mountains and lakes, some are hard to control in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu barbarians left and right have always fled—some into lakes and hills, some to raid where none can hold them.

sentences.zh: 若凶渠黠黨，有須翦除者，便可撲掃，以清疆界。

translations.literal: If there are vicious ringleaders and cunning factions that must be cut down, you may sweep them to clear the borders.
translations.idiomatic: If vicious ringleaders must be cut down, sweep them and clear the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如其強狡憑阻，未易致力者，亦不煩肆兵。

translations.literal: If they rely on strength and cunning and hold defiles not easy to attack, do not trouble to deploy troops in vain.
translations.idiomatic: If they hold defiles you cannot take without waste, do not waste troops on them.

sentences.zh: 凱旋遲近，不復委曲。

translations.literal: Near or far for the triumphal return—no further details.
translations.idiomatic: When you come home, near or far, I leave to you."

sentences.zh: 」英表曰：「臣奉辭伐罪，志殄逋寇，想敵量攻，期至二月將末三月之初，理在必克。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized: "Your servant received orders to punish crime, my will to destroy the fleeing rebels; measuring the enemy and attacking, I expect from the end of the second month into early third month—by reason it must be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied: "I came to punish rebels and meant to destroy them; gauging the foe, I set the end of the second month or the start of the third for victory.

sentences.zh: 但自此月一日以來，霖雨連併，可謂天違人願。

translations.literal: But from the first day of this month rain has joined day on day—one may say Heaven goes against men's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the first of this month rain has not stopped—Heaven against our wish.

sentences.zh: 然王者行師，舉動不易，不可以少致睽淹，便生異議。

translations.literal: Yet when the king's army marches, movement is not easy; one cannot for a little obstruction and delay at once raise dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Still, a king's army does not turn for a little mud; we must not quarrel over a short delay.

sentences.zh: 臣亦諦思。

translations.literal: Your servant has also thought deeply.
translations.idiomatic: I have thought hard on this.

sentences.zh: 若入三月已後，天晴地燥，憑陵是常。

translations.literal: If after the third month the sky clears and the ground dries, riding over them will be the rule.
translations.idiomatic: If March brings clear skies and dry ground, we can ride them down.

sentences.zh: 如其連雨仍接，不得進攻者，臣已更高邵陽之橋，防其汎突。

translations.literal: If rain still joins and we cannot attack, your servant has already raised the Shaoyang bridge higher to guard against flooding assault.
translations.idiomatic: If the rains continue and we cannot attack, I have raised the Shaoyang bridge against flood assault.

sentences.zh: 意外洪長，慮其破橋，臣亦部分造船，復於鍾離城隨水狹處，營造浮橋，至三月中旬，橋必克成。

translations.literal: Should the waters rise beyond expectation and I fear the bridge will break, your servant has also assigned ship-building; again at Zhongli where the water narrows I am building a pontoon bridge—by mid-third month the bridge will surely be finished.
translations.idiomatic: If the flood breaks the bridge, I am building boats and a pontoon at the narrows by Zhongli—by mid-March it will stand.

sentences.zh: 晴則攻騰，雨則圍守，水陸二圖，以得為限。

translations.literal: Clear weather then storm assault; rain then siege and hold—two plans by land and water, taking success as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun—we storm; rain—we siege: land and water, two plans, success our only measure.

sentences.zh: 實願朝廷特開遠略，少復賜寬，假以日月，無使為山之功，中途而廢。

translations.literal: Truly I wish the court especially to open a far-reaching plan, grant a little more indulgence, lend days and months, and not let the work of moving mountains stop halfway.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the court to look far, grant more time, and not abandon a mountain's labor halfway."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「大軍野次，已成勞久，攻守之方，理可豫見。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The great army camps in the field and has already grown weary long; attack and defense—the principle can be foreseen in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered: "The host has camped long; attack and defense should be plain.

sentences.zh: 比頻得啟，制勝不過暮春，及省後表，復期孟夏之末。

translations.literal: Recently your memorials repeatedly said victory would be no later than late spring; when I examined the later memorial, again the term was set for the end of early summer.
translations.idiomatic: Your letters promised victory by late spring; the next set midsummer.

sentences.zh: 彼土蒸濘，無宜久淹。

translations.literal: That land is steamy and muddy—not fit to linger long.
translations.idiomatic: That country is steam and mud—not fit to linger in.

sentences.zh: 勢雖必取，乃將軍之深計；

translations.literal: Though the situation must be taken—that is the general's deep plan;
translations.idiomatic: Taking the city is your deep plan;

sentences.zh: 兵久力殆，亦朝廷之所憂。

translations.literal: troops long deployed, strength exhausted—that is also what the court worries over.
translations.idiomatic: troops long abroad and spent—that is what the court fears.

sentences.zh: 故遣主書曹道往觀軍勢，使還，一一具聞。

translations.literal: Therefore Director of Documents Cao Dao is sent to observe the army's condition; when he returns, report each point in full.
translations.idiomatic: I send Director of Documents Cao Dao to see your host; let him report everything."

sentences.zh: 」[3]及道還，英猶表云「可克」。

translations.literal: [3] When Dao returned, Ying still memorialized saying "it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: [3] When Dao returned, Ying still wrote that the city could be taken.

sentences.zh: 四月，水盛破橋，英及諸將狼狽奔走，士眾沒者十有五六。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the waters swelled and broke the bridge; Ying and the generals fled in disarray, and of the soldiers and masses drowned, one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month flood broke the bridge; Ying and his officers fled in disorder, and one or two soldiers in ten drowned.

sentences.zh: 英至揚州，遣使送節及衣冠、貂蟬、章綬。

translations.literal: Ying reached Yangzhou and sent envoys to deliver the staff and regalia, marten cap, and seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou he sent back his staff, robes, marten cap, and seals.

sentences.zh: 詔以付典。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them delivered to the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent them to the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 有司奏英經算失圖，案劾處死，詔恕死為民。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Ying's calculations missed the plan and impeached him for death; an edict pardoned death and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries impeached him for failed strategy and sought death; the throne spared his life and made him a commoner.

sentences.zh: 後京兆王愉反，英復王封，邑一千戶，除使持節，假征東將軍、都督冀州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Later when Prince Yu of Jingzhao rebelled, Ying's princely title was restored with a fief of one thousand households; he was made bearer of the staff, acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Area Commander of military affairs in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao rebelled, Ying's title was restored at one thousand households; he was given the staff as acting General Who Pacifies the East and commander of Ji.

sentences.zh: 英未發而冀州已平。

translations.literal: Before Ying set out, Ji Province was already pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched, Ji was already quiet.

sentences.zh: 時郢州治中督榮祖潛引蕭衍軍，以義陽應之，三關之戍，並據城降衍。

translations.literal: At that time Yingzhou Administrator Supervisor Rongzu secretly led Xiao Yan's army; Yiyang answered them, and the garrisons of the Three Passes all held their cities and submitted to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou supervisor Rongzu secretly brought in Xiao Yan's troops; Yiyang joined them, and every Three Passes garrison surrendered.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史婁悅嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Yingzhou Inspector Lou Yue defended the city with a closed ring.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Lou Yue shut the walls and held on.

sentences.zh: 懸瓠城民白早生等殺豫州刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。

translations.literal: The people of Xuancheng, Bai Zaosheng and others, killed Yu Province Inspector Sima Yue, held the south of the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuancheng, Bai Zaosheng and others killed Inspector Sima Yue, seized the south wall, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 衍將齊苟仁率眾守懸瓠。

translations.literal: Yan's general Qi Gouren led a host to hold Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Qi Gouren held Xuancheng with an army.

sentences.zh: 悅子尚華陽公主，并為所劫。

translations.literal: Yue's son had married the Princess of Huayang and was also seized as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son, who had married the Princess of Huayang, was taken hostage as well.

sentences.zh: 詔英使持節、都督南征諸軍事、假征南將軍，出自汝南。

translations.literal: An edict made Ying bearer of the staff, Area Commander of the Southern Campaign armies, and acting General Who Pacifies the South, setting out from Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was ordered out from Runan with the staff, command of the southern campaign, and acting General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 世宗引英謂之曰：「婁悅綏御失和，銓衡闇於簡授，故使郢民引寇，關戍外奔，義陽孤窘，有倒懸之切。

translations.literal: Shizong received Ying and said to him: "Lou Yue's soothing and control lost harmony; scales and balance were dark in brief appointment—therefore Ying's people drew in the enemy, pass garrisons fled outward, Yiyang stands lonely and pressed, with the urgency of hanging upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told him: "Lou Yue lost his grip; the wrong men were posted, so Ying drew in the foe, the passes emptied, and Yiyang hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 王國之邵虎，威名宿震，故屈王親總元戎，掃清氛穢。

translations.literal: The state's Shao Hu of old, might and name long shaken—therefore we bend the prince to take command of the main army in person and sweep clear the foul air.
translations.idiomatic: You are our Shao Hu—your name alone should clear the air. I bend a prince to lead the host and sweep the filth away.

sentences.zh: 昔衞霍以匈奴之故，居無寧歲，今南疆不靖，王不得以屢勞為辭也。

translations.literal: In old times Wei and Huo, because of the Xiongnu, had no year of peace; now the southern border is not quiet—you, prince, may not decline because of repeated toil."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing knew no peaceful year while the Xiongnu lived; the south is unquiet—you may not refuse because you are weary."

sentences.zh: 」英對曰：「臣才非韓白，識闇孫吳，徒以宗室之長，頻荷推轂之寄。

translations.literal: Ying replied: "Your servant's talent is not Han Xin or Bai Qi; my knowledge is dimmer than Sun Wu's or Wu Qi's—only as eldest of the imperial clan I have repeatedly borne the trust of being pushed in the chariot shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Ying answered: "I am no Han Xin or Bai Qi, no Sun Wu or Wu Qi—only as senior prince I have been trusted again and again with the chariot pole.

sentences.zh: 規略淺短，失律喪師，宜章子反之戮，以謝天下。

translations.literal: My strategy shallow and short, losing the statutes and losing the army—I ought to bear the punishment of Zengzi's son in reverse, to answer to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: My plans were shallow; I lost the law and lost the army—I ought to die like Zengzi's son, to answer the world.

sentences.zh: 陛下慈深念屨，愛等鍾牛，使臣得同荀伯，再生明世，誓追孟氏，以報復為期。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's mercy is deep, mindful even of worn sandals, love equal to a bell-ox—your servant may be like Xun Bo, reborn in a bright age, vowing to follow Meng Ke and make repayment the term.
translations.idiomatic: Your mercy is deep—you spare even worn shoes, love me like a sacrificial ox; let me be Xun Bo reborn, follow Mencius, and repay you.

sentences.zh: 關郢微寇，何足平殄，滅賊方略，已在臣目中，願陛下勿勞聖慮也。

translations.literal: The slight rebels of the passes and Ying—what worth to pacify and destroy? The plan to destroy the rebels is already in your servant's eye; I wish Your Majesty not to trouble the sage worry."
translations.idiomatic: These border fleas are nothing; I already see how to crush them—trouble yourself no further."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「截彼東南，再清隨楚，所望於將軍。

translations.literal: Shizong said: "Cutting off their southeast, again clearing Sui and Chu—that is what is hoped from the general.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said: "I look to you to cut the southeast and clear Sui and Chu again.

sentences.zh: 鍾離一眚，豈足以損大德。

translations.literal: Zhongli's one mishap—how could it damage great virtue?
translations.idiomatic: One disaster at Zhongli cannot stain great merit.

sentences.zh: 今王董彼三軍，朕無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Now the prince directs those three armies; I have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Lead the three armies—I have no fear."

sentences.zh: 世宗以邢巒頻破早生，詔英南赴義陽。

translations.literal: Shizong, because Xing Luan had repeatedly broken Zaosheng, ordered Ying south to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xing Luan had already broken Zaosheng, Shizong sent Ying south to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 英以眾少，累表請軍，世宗弗許。

translations.literal: Ying, because his troops were few, repeatedly memorialized asking for reinforcements; Shizong did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, short of men, begged for troops; Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 而英輒與邢巒分兵共攻懸瓠，克之，乃引軍而進。

translations.literal: Yet Ying at once joined Xing Luan in dividing troops to attack Xuancheng together; they took it, and then led the army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he joined Xing Luan, took Xuancheng together, and marched on.

sentences.zh: 初苟仁之據懸瓠，衍寧朔將軍張道凝等率眾據楚城，聞英將至，棄城南走。

translations.literal: When Gouren first held Xuancheng, Yan's Pacify-the-North General Zhang Daoning and others led troops to hold Chucheng; hearing Ying was coming, they abandoned the city and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: While Gouren held Xuancheng, Zhang Daoning held Chucheng; hearing Ying approached, they fled south.

sentences.zh: 英追擊，斬道凝及衍虎賁中郎曹苦生，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Ying pursued, beheaded Daoning and Yan's Tiger Guard Central Officer Cao Kusheng, and captured their entire host.
translations.idiomatic: Ying ran them down, killed Daoning and Cao Kusheng of the Tiger Guard, and took every man.

sentences.zh: 既次義陽，將取三關，英策之曰：「三關相須如左右手，若克一關，兩關不待攻而定。

translations.literal: Having halted at Yiyang, about to take the Three Passes, Ying calculated: "The Three Passes depend on one another like left and right hands; if one pass is taken, the two passes need not be attacked and are settled.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiyang he planned the Three Passes: "They need each other like two hands—take one, and the other two fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 攻難不如攻易，東關易攻，宜須先取，即黃石公所謂戰如風發，攻如河決。
