translations.literal: To attack the hard is not as good as attacking the easy; the East Pass is easy to attack—you should first take it, exactly what the Yellow Stone Elder called: battle like wind rising, assault like a river breaking its banks."
translations.idiomatic: Strike the easy, not the hard. The East Pass is weak—take it first, as the Yellow Stone Elder said: fight like wind, strike like a broken river."

sentences.zh: 」英恐其并力於東，乃使長史李華率五統向西關，分其兵勢。

translations.literal: Ying feared they would combine strength on the east; he therefore sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five army groups toward the West Pass to divide their force.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a concentration in the east, he sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five columns against the West Pass to split their strength.

sentences.zh: 身督諸軍向東關。

translations.literal: He himself supervised the armies toward the East Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He led the main force to the East Pass.

sentences.zh: 先是，馬仙琕使雲騎將軍馬廣率眾拒屯於長薄，軍主胡文超別屯松峴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Xianbi had sent Cloud-Cavalry General Ma Guang with a host to resist and encamp at Changbo; Army Commander Hu Wenchao separately encamped at Songxian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ma Xianbi had posted Ma Guang at Changbo and Hu Wenchao at Songxian.

sentences.zh: 英至長薄，馬廣夜遁入於武陽，英進師攻之。

translations.literal: When Ying reached Changbo, Ma Guang fled by night into Wuyang; Ying advanced his army to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At Changbo, Ma Guang slipped away by night into Wuyang; Ying followed and besieged him.

sentences.zh: 聞衍遣其冠軍將軍彭瓫生、驃騎將軍徐超秀援武陽。

translations.literal: Hearing Yan had sent its Champion General Peng Fusheng and Flying Cavalry General Xu Chaoxiu to rescue Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Yan's Champion Peng Fusheng and Flying Cavalry Xu Chaoxiu were marching to relieve Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 英乃緩軍，曰：「縱之使入此城，吾先曾觀其形勢，易攻耳，吾取之如拾遺也。

translations.literal: Ying therefore slowed the army and said: "Let them enter this city—I once observed its terrain; it is easy to attack. I take it like picking up something dropped."
translations.idiomatic: Ying slowed his march. "Let them in—I know that ground; it is easy. I will take it as one picks up what was dropped."

sentences.zh: 」諸將未之信。

translations.literal: The generals did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: His officers did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 瓫生等既入武陽，英促圍攻之，六日而廣等降。

translations.literal: When Fusheng and the rest had entered Wuyang, Ying pressed the siege; in six days Ma Guang and the rest surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fusheng was inside, Ying pressed the siege; in six days Ma Guang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是進擊黃峴，衍太子左衞率李元履棄城奔竄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced to strike Huangxian; Yan's Crown Prince Left Guard Leader Li Yuanyi abandoned the city and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Huangxian; Yan's Left Guard Leader Li Yuanyi fled.

sentences.zh: 又討西關，衍司州刺史馬仙琕亦即退走，果如英策。

translations.literal: He again attacked the West Pass; Yan's Provincial Inspector Ma Xianbi also at once retreated—exactly as Ying had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: He took the West Pass; Ma Xianbi fled at once—just as Ying had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 凡擒其大將六人，支將二十人，卒七千，米四十萬石，軍資稱是。

translations.literal: In all he captured six of their great generals, twenty sub-generals, seven thousand soldiers, four hundred thousand piculs of grain, and military stores in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: He took six great generals, twenty subordinates, seven thousand men, four hundred thousand piculs of grain, and full stores.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 永平三年，英薨，給東園祕器、朝服一具、帛七百匹，贈司徒公，諡曰獻武王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongping, Ying died; he was granted the Eastern Garden secret vessels, one set of court robes, seven hundred bolts of silk, posthumously made Duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Prince Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping year 3 he died; the court gave secret funeral gear, court robes, seven hundred bolts of silk, posthumous rank as Duke of the Secretariat, and the title Prince Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 英五子。

translations.literal: Ying had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had five sons.

sentences.zh: 英 子 攸

translations.literal: Ying — son — You
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son: You

sentences.zh: 攸，字玄興，東宮洗馬。

translations.literal: You, styled Xuanxing, was Eastern Palace Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: You, courtesy name Xuanxing, served as Eastern Palace Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 早卒，贈散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He died young; posthumously made Scattered Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died young and was posthumously made Scattered Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 攸 弟 中山文莊王熙

translations.literal: You — younger brother — Xi, Prince Wenzhuang of Zhongshan
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother: Xi, Prince Wenzhuang of Zhongshan

sentences.zh: （附子 景獻 仲獻 叔獻 叔仁 ／ 叔仁 子 琳）

translations.literal: (Attached sons: Jingxian, Zhongxian, Shuxian, Shuren / Shuren — son — Lin)
translations.idiomatic: (Sons: Jingxian, Zhongxian, Shuxian, Shuren; Shuren's son: Lin)

sentences.zh: 攸弟熙，字真興。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Xi, styled Zhenxing.
translations.idiomatic: You's brother Xi, courtesy name Zhenxing.

sentences.zh: 好學，俊爽有文才，聲著於世，然輕躁浮動。

translations.literal: He loved learning, was handsome and bright with literary talent, his fame resounding in the age—yet he was frivolous, rash, and restless.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, was brilliant and literary, famed in his day—yet frivolous and restless.

sentences.zh: 英深慮非保家之主，常欲廢之，立第四子略為世子，宗議不聽，略又固請，乃止。

translations.literal: Ying deeply worried he was not fit to preserve the house; he often wished to disinherit him and establish the fourth son Lüe as heir, but clan opinion would not listen, and Lüe also firmly declined—thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ying feared he would ruin the house and tried to make his fourth son Lüe heir; the clan refused, and Lüe refused too—so he desisted.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎，延昌二年襲封，累遷兼將作大匠，拜太常少卿、給事黃門侍郎，尋轉光祿勳。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Attendant; in the second year of Yanxi he inherited the fief, was promoted in succession to Acting Director of Palace Construction, made Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and Palace Attendant Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary, and soon transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a secretariat attendant, inherited in Yanxi year 2, rose through construction and ritual posts to Yellow Gate attendant-in-ordinary, then Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 時領軍于忠執政。

translations.literal: At the time Area Commander-in-chief Yu Zhong held power.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong, area commander-in-chief, held the government.

sentences.zh: 熙，忠之壻也，故歲中驟遷。

translations.literal: Xi was Yu Zhong's son-in-law; therefore within the year he was suddenly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Zhong's son-in-law and was promoted with unnatural speed.

sentences.zh: 尋除平西將軍、東秦州刺史，進號安西將軍，祕書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Pacify-the-West General and Eastern Qinzhou Inspector, advanced in title to Pacify-the-Qin General and Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Pacify-the-West General and Eastern Qinzhou inspector, then Pacify-the-Qin General and palace librarian.

sentences.zh: 尋以本將軍授相州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon with that general's title he was given Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made inspector of Xiangzhou under the same rank.

sentences.zh: 熙以七月入治，其日大風寒雨，凍死者二十餘人，驢馬數十匹。

translations.literal: Xi entered to govern in the seventh month; that day great wind and cold rain—more than twenty men froze to death, and several tens of donkeys and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He took office in the seventh month; that day a gale and cold rain killed more than twenty men and dozens of pack animals.

sentences.zh: 熙聞其祖父前事，心惡之。

translations.literal: Xi heard of his grandfather's earlier affair and hated it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded on his grandfather's fate.

sentences.zh: 又有蛆生其庭。

translations.literal: Maggots also bred in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Maggots bred in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 初，熙兄弟並為清河王懌所昵，及劉騰、元叉隔絕二宮，矯詔殺懌，熙乃起兵，上表曰：「臣聞安危無常，時有休否。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi and his brothers had all been favored by Prince Yi of Qinghe; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha cut off the Two Palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi thereupon raised troops and memorialized: "Your servant has heard that safety and danger have no constancy—times have their rest and decline.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and his brothers had been close to Prince Yi of Qinghe; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha walled off the palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi raised troops and wrote: "Safety and danger have no fixed hour.

sentences.zh: 臣早屬休明，晚逢多難。

translations.literal: Your servant early belonged to a bright age, late met many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: I was born to brightness and met only hardship.

sentences.zh: 自皇基綿茂，九葉承光，高祖、世宗，徽明相襲。

translations.literal: Since the imperial foundation has been lush and nine leaves have borne glory, Gaozu and Shizong, emblems bright succeeding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations have flourished since Gaozu and Shizong.

sentences.zh: 皇太后聖敬自天，德同馬鄧；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's sacred reverence comes from Heaven, virtue equal to Ma and Deng;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's virtue equals Ma and Deng;

sentences.zh: 至尊神叡纂御，神鑒燭遠。

translations.literal: His Majesty's divine wisdom inherits the throne, divine mirror shining far.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty rules with divine sight.

sentences.zh: 四海晏如，八表歸化。

translations.literal: Within the four seas all is calm; the eight directions return to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is calm; the eight directions submit.

sentences.zh: 而領軍將軍元叉寵藉外親，叨榮左右，豺狼為心，飽便反嚙。

translations.literal: Yet Area Commander Yuan Cha, relying on favor through outside kin, greedily honored at the left and right, wolf heart—fed full, he turns to bite.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan Cha, favored through kin, sits at the emperor's side with a wolf's heart—fed full, he bites.

sentences.zh: 遂使二宮阻隔，溫凊闕禮，又太傅清河王橫被屠害。

translations.literal: He made the Two Palaces cut off, warm greetings and care lacking in ritual; again the Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe was slaughtered across.
translations.idiomatic: He walled off the Two Palaces, ended the rites of filial care, and had Prince Yi of Qinghe butchered.

sentences.zh: 致使忠臣烈士，喪氣闕庭；

translations.literal: He made loyal ministers and martyrs lose spirit at the court gate;
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men lost heart at the gate;

sentences.zh: 親賢宗戚，憤恨內外。

translations.literal: kin and worthies of the clan, anger and hate within and without.
translations.idiomatic: kin and worthies seethed within and without.

sentences.zh: 妄指鹿馬，孰能踰之；

translations.literal: Pointing at deer and calling them horses—who can go beyond this?
translations.idiomatic: Calling deer horses—who can outdo that?

sentences.zh: 王董權逼，方此非譬。

translations.literal: Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo forcing power—compared with this, no likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo beside this are nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣仰瞻雲闕，泣血而生，以細草不除，將為爛漫，況叉悖逆如此，孰可忍之！

translations.literal: Your servant looks up at the cloud gate, weeping blood while alive—if fine grass is not cleared it will become rank growth; how much more when Cha's rebellion is thus—who can bear it!
translations.idiomatic: I weep blood beneath the cloud gate—uncut grass becomes a jungle; Cha's crime is worse—who can bear it?

sentences.zh: 臣忝籍枝蕚，思盡力命，碎首屠肝，甘之若薺。

translations.literal: Your servant, bearing branch and calyx of the tree, thinks to exhaust strength and life, smash head and butcher liver—sweet as shepherd's purse.
translations.idiomatic: I am of the imperial branch and will spend life and liver gladly.

sentences.zh: 今輒起義兵，實甲八萬，大徒既進，文武爭先，與并州刺史、城陽王徽，恒州刺史、廣陽王淵，徐州刺史、齊王蕭寶夤等，同以今月十四日俱發。

translations.literal: Now I have raised righteous troops in fact, armor eight myriad; the great host already advances, civil and military vie to be first—with Bingzhou Inspector Prince Hui of Chengyang, Hengzhou Inspector Prince Yuan of Guangyang, Xuzhou Inspector Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin, and others, all to set out together on the fourteenth of this month.
translations.idiomatic: I raise eight myriad men in arms; with Prince Hui of Chengyang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang, and Xiao Baoyin of Qi I march on the fourteenth.

sentences.zh: 庶仰憑祖宗之靈，俯罄義夫之命，掃翦兇醜，更清京邑。

translations.literal: I hope to lean on the spirits of the ancestors, bow and exhaust the righteous men's lives, sweep the vicious and ugly, and again clear the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By our ancestors' shades we will scour the villains and clear the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣親總三軍，星邁赴難，置兵溫城，伏聽天旨。

translations.literal: Your servant personally commands the three armies, stars hurrying to the crisis, placing troops at Warm City, lying low to hear Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: I lead three armies to Warm City and wait on Heaven's word.

sentences.zh: 王公宰輔，或世著忠烈，或宿佩恩顧，如能同力，翦除元叉，使太后至尊忻然奉對者，臣即解甲散兵，赴謝朝闕。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and aides—some famed for loyalty through generations, some long cherishing grace and regard—if you can join strength and cut down Yuan Cha, so that the Empress Dowager and His Majesty may gladly face one another, your servant will at once unarm and disband the host and go to answer at the court gate.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers famed for loyalty—join me, cut down Cha, restore the Empress Dowager and the Son of Heaven to one another, and I will lay down arms at the gate.

sentences.zh: 臣雖才乖昔人，位居蕃屏，寧容坐觀姦醜，虛受榮祿哉！

translations.literal: Though your servant's talent falls short of men of old, my place is the frontier screen of the realm—how can I sit and watch vicious ugliness and vainly receive glory and salary!"
translations.idiomatic: I hold a frontier fief—how can I watch villains and still draw salary?"

sentences.zh: 」熙兵起甫十日，為其長史柳元章、別駕游荊、魏郡太守李孝怡率諸城人，鼓譟而入，殺熙左右四十餘人，執熙，置之高樓，并其子弟。

translations.literal: Xi's troops had risen only ten days when his Chief Clerk Liu Yuanzhang, Vice Director You Jing, and Wei Commandery Governor Li Xiaoyi led the people of the cities, beating drums and clamoring as they entered, killed more than forty of Xi's attendants, seized Xi, placed him on a high tower, and together with his sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after he rose, his chief clerk, vice director, and Wei governor led the townsfolk in, killed forty of his men, seized Xi and his sons, and held them in a tower.

sentences.zh: 叉遣尚書左丞盧同斬之於鄴街，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Cha sent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Tong to behead him in the Ye street and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent Lu Tong to behead him in the streets of Ye and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 始熙妃于氏知熙必敗，不從其謀，自初哭泣不絕，至於熙死。

translations.literal: From the first Xi's consort the Lady Yu knew Xi would fail and did not follow his plot; from the beginning she wept without cease until Xi's death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yu knew he would fail, refused his plot, and wept without stop until he died.

sentences.zh: 熙臨刑為五言詩，示其僚吏曰：「義實動君子，主辱死忠臣。

translations.literal: At execution Xi composed a five-character poem and showed it to his clerks and officials: "Righteousness truly moves the gentleman; the lord's disgrace—death for the loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he wrote five lines for his staff: "Righteousness stirs the noble heart; a lord's shame calls the loyal man to die.

sentences.zh: 何以明是節，將解七尺身。

translations.literal: How to make clear this integrity? About to untie seven feet of body."
translations.idiomatic: How shall I show this faith? I give up seven feet of flesh."

sentences.zh: 」與知友別曰：「平生方寸心，殷勤屬知己。

translations.literal: Parting from close friends he said: "All my life one square inch of heart, earnestness entrusted to the knowing friend.
translations.idiomatic: To friends he said: "All my life one heart I gave to friends.

sentences.zh: 從今一銷化，悲傷無極已。」

translations.literal: From now one melting away—grief without limit."
translations.idiomatic: Now it melts away—grief without end."

sentences.zh: 熙既蕃王之貴，加有文學，好奇愛異，交結偉俊，風氣甚高，名美當世，先達後進，多造其門。

translations.literal: Xi, being noble among the frontier princes, moreover had literature; he loved the strange and cherished the different, formed ties with great and handsome men, his air very lofty, his name beautiful in the age—elders before and juniors after, many came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier prince and a man of letters, he sought out brilliant company; the age praised him, and many came to his door.

sentences.zh: 始熙之鎮鄴也，知友才學之士袁翻、李琰、李神儁、王誦兄弟、裴敬憲等咸餞於河梁，賦詩告別。

translations.literal: When Xi first went to govern Ye, talented literary men Yuan Fan, Li Yan, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others all saw him off at River Bridge, composing poems in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When he left for Ye, Yuan Fan, Li Shenjun, the Wang brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others saw him off at River Bridge with poems.

sentences.zh: 及熙將死，復與知故書曰：「吾與弟並蒙皇太后知遇，兄據大州，弟則入侍，殷勤言色，恩同慈母。

translations.literal: When Xi was about to die he again wrote to old friends: "I and my younger brother both received the Empress Dowager's knowing encounter; elder brother held a great province, younger brother then entered attendance—earnest words and color, grace like a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before death he wrote to friends: "My brother and I were cherished by the Empress Dowager—he in a great province, I at court—treated like sons.

sentences.zh: 今皇太后見廢北宮，太傅清河王橫受屠酷，主上幼年，獨在前殿。

translations.literal: Now the Empress Dowager is deposed in the North Palace; the Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe was slaughtered across; the lord is young, alone in the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Now she is confined in the North Palace, Prince Yi was butchered, and the boy emperor sits alone.

sentences.zh: 君親如此，無以自安，故率兵民建大義於天下。

translations.literal: Lord and kin thus—I cannot be at peace; therefore I lead soldiers and people to raise great righteousness under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I could not rest; I raised arms in the name of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 但智力淺短，旋見囚執，上慚朝廷，下愧相知。

translations.literal: But my strength and wit shallow and short—soon I was seized; above I shame the court, below I fail my friends.
translations.idiomatic: My wits were short; I was seized at once—shame to the court, shame to you.

sentences.zh: 本以名義干心，不得不爾，流腸碎首，復何言哉！

translations.literal: Originally it was fame and duty that moved my heart—I could not do otherwise; guts streaming, head smashed—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Duty drove me; guts spill—what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 昔李斯憶上蔡黃犬，陸機想華亭鶴唳，豈不以恍惚無際，一去不還者乎？

translations.literal: In old times Li Si remembered the yellow dog of Shangcai; Lu Ji thought of the crane's cry at Huating—was it not because illusion has no bound, once gone never to return?
translations.idiomatic: Li Si remembered Shangcai's yellow dog; Lu Ji the crane at Huating—gone, never back.

sentences.zh: 今欲對秋月，臨春風，藉芳草，蔭花樹，廣召名勝，賦詩洛濱，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Now I wish to face the autumn moon, meet the spring wind, lean on fragrant grass, shade flowering trees, broadly summon famous guests, compose poems on the Luo shore—can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: I will not face the moon, the wind, the grass, the trees, or poems on the Luo again.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，各敬爾宜，為國為身，善勗名節，立功立事，為身而已，吾何言哉！

translations.literal: All you gentlemen, each respect your proper conduct; for the state and for the body, well urge fame and integrity, establish merit and affairs—for the body alone—what have I to say!
translations.idiomatic: Live for the state and for yourselves; make merit; I have no more words."

sentences.zh: 」時人憐之。

translations.literal: People of the time pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Men pitied him.

sentences.zh: 又熙於任城王澄薨前，夢有人告之曰：「任城當死。

translations.literal: Also, before Prince Cheng of Ren's death, Xi dreamed someone told him: "Ren will die.
translations.idiomatic: Before Prince Cheng of Ren died, Xi dreamed a voice said, "Ren will die.

sentences.zh: 死後二百日外，君亦不免。

translations.literal: Two hundred days after his death, you too will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred days later you will not escape.

sentences.zh: 若其不信，試看任城家。

translations.literal: If you do not believe it, try looking at Ren's house."
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt it, look at Ren's mansion."

sentences.zh: 」熙夢中顧瞻任城第舍，四面牆崩，無遺堵焉。

translations.literal: In the dream Xi looked back at Ren's residence; the walls on four sides collapsed—no remaining parapet.
translations.idiomatic: In the dream he saw Ren's walls fall on every side to the ground.

sentences.zh: 熙惡之，覺而以告所親。

translations.literal: Xi hated it; waking, he told those close to him.
translations.idiomatic: He woke in dread and told his kin.

sentences.zh: 及熙之死也，果如所夢。

translations.literal: When Xi died, it was indeed as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, it was as the dream had said.

sentences.zh: 兄弟三人，每從英征伐，在軍貪暴，或因迎降逐北，至有斬殺無辜，多增首級，以為功狀。

translations.literal: The three brothers, whenever they followed Ying on campaign, in the army were greedy and violent; sometimes in welcoming surrender and pursuing the defeated they would even behead the innocent, often adding to the head count to make merit reports.
translations.idiomatic: All three followed Ying to war and grew greedy and cruel—sometimes killing the innocent among surrendering fugitives to pad their body counts.

sentences.zh: 又于忠之誣郭祚、裴植也，忠意未決害之，由熙勸奬，遂至極法，世以為冤。

translations.literal: Also in Yu Zhong's framing of Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Zhong's mind had not yet decided to kill them—through Xi's urging and encouragement they came to the extreme penalty; the age considered it a wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zhong framed Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Xi urged him on to execution—the world called it injustice.

sentences.zh: 及熙之禍，議者以為有報應焉。

translations.literal: When Xi's calamity came, debaters held there was retribution.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi fell, men said it was retribution.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，贈使持節、都督冀定瀛相幽五州諸軍事、大將軍、太尉公、冀州刺史，增本封一千戶，諡曰文莊王。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ling restored government, she posthumously made him bearer of the staff, Area Commander of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, and You provinces, Grand General, Grand Commandant, Ji Province Inspector, added one thousand households to his original fief, posthumous title Prince Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling returned to power, she restored him as commander of five provinces, Grand General, Grand Commandant, added a thousand households, and titled him Prince Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 長子景獻，次仲獻，次叔獻，並與熙同被害。

translations.literal: The eldest son Jingxian, next Zhongxian, next Shuxian—all were killed together with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian, Zhongxian, and Shuxian died with him.

sentences.zh: 後贈景獻中軍將軍、青州刺史，葬以王禮；

translations.literal: Later Jingxian was posthumously made Central Army General and Qingzhou Inspector, buried with princely rites;
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian was later made Central Army General and Qingzhou inspector and buried as a prince;

sentences.zh: 仲獻左將軍、兗州刺史；

translations.literal: Zhongxian, Left General and Yanzhou Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian as Left General and Yanzhou inspector;

sentences.zh: 叔獻右將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shuxian, Right General and Qizhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian as Right General and Qizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 叔獻弟叔仁，以年幼獲全，與母于氏徙朔州。

translations.literal: Shuxian's younger brother Shuren, because he was young, was spared whole, and with his mother the Lady Yu was moved to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Young Shuren was spared and sent to Shuozhou with his mother Lady Yu.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，靈太后詔叔仁歸京師，還其財宅，襲先爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang the Empress Dowager Ling ordered Shuren to return to the capital, restored his property and residence, and he inherited the former title.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year 1 Ling ordered Shuren home, restored his estate, and let him inherit.

sentences.zh: 除征虜將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Regular Attendant, Direct Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Subdues the Barbarians and regular attendant for direct transmission.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遇害於河陰，贈衞大將軍、儀同三司、并州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he met disaster at Heyin; posthumously made Guard General, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Bingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession he died at Heyin and was posthumously made Guard General with honor equal to the Three Dukes and inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子琳，襲。

translations.literal: His son Lin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, the fief was reduced as custom required.

sentences.zh: 熙 弟 誘

translations.literal: Xi — younger brother — You
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother: You

sentences.zh: （附子 始伯）

translations.literal: (Attached son: Shibo)
translations.idiomatic: (Son: Shibo)

sentences.zh: 熙弟誘，字惠興。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother You, styled Huixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's brother You, courtesy name Huixing.

sentences.zh: 自員外郎稍遷通直郎、太子中庶子、征虜將軍、衞尉少卿，出為右將軍、南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: From Outer Palace Attendant he was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant, Crown Prince Central Palace Attendant, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Guards, and went out as Right General and Southern Qinzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from outer attendant to crown prince's central attendant, Guard vice director, then Right General and Southern Qinzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 叉斬之於岐州，妻子得不坐。

translations.literal: Cha beheaded him in Qizhou; wife and children were not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Cha executed him in Qizhou; his family was spared.

sentences.zh: 追贈車騎大將軍、雍州刺史，後贈儀同三司，追封都昌縣開國伯，食邑八百戶，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yongzhou Inspector; later posthumously made Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, enfeoffed as founding Earl of Duchang with eight hundred households, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yongzhou inspector, later equal to the Three Dukes, founding Earl of Duchang with eight hundred households, titled Gong.

sentences.zh: 子始伯，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shibo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 給事中。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, the title was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 誘 弟 東平文貞王略

translations.literal: You — younger brother — Lüe, Prince Wenzhen of Dongping
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother: Lüe, Prince Wenzhen of Dongping

sentences.zh: （附子 景式）

translations.literal: (Attached son: Jingshi)
translations.idiomatic: (Son: Jingshi)

sentences.zh: 誘弟略，字儁興。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Lüe, styled Junxing.
translations.idiomatic: You's brother Lüe, courtesy name Junxing.

sentences.zh: 才氣劣於熙，而有和邃之譽。

translations.literal: His talent and air were inferior to Xi's, yet he had a reputation for harmony and depth.
translations.idiomatic: Less brilliant than Xi, he was known for calm depth.

sentences.zh: 自員外郎稍遷羽林監、通直散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: From Outer Palace Attendant he was gradually promoted to Feathered Forest Supervisor, Regular Attendant Scattered Cavalier, Champion General, and Palace Attendant Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the feathered forest, scattered cavalier, champion general, to Yellow Gate attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌死後，叉黜略為懷朔鎮副將。

translations.literal: After Prince Yi of Qinghe died, Cha demoted Lüe to deputy commander of Huaishuo Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Yi's death, Cha demoted him to deputy at Huaishuo Garrison.

sentences.zh: 未及赴任，會熙起兵，與略書來去。

translations.literal: Before he could go to his post, Xi raised troops and letters went back and forth between him and Lüe.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took post, Xi rebelled and letters passed between the brothers.

sentences.zh: 尋值熙敗，略遂潛行，自託舊識河內司馬始賓。

translations.literal: Soon Xi failed; Lüe then traveled in secret, entrusting himself to an old acquaintance, Interior Minister of Henei Shi Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi fell, Lüe fled in secret to Shi Bin, interior minister of Henei.

sentences.zh: 始賓便為荻筏，夜與略俱渡盟津，詣上黨屯留縣栗法光。

translations.literal: Shi Bin then made a reed raft; by night he and Lüe together crossed the Meng Ford and went to Li Faguang of Tunliu in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Bin built a reed raft; by night they crossed the Meng Ford to Li Faguang at Tunliu in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 法光素敦信義，忻而納之。

translations.literal: Faguang had always been thick in faith and righteousness; gladly he received him.
translations.idiomatic: Faguang, a man of faith, welcomed him gladly.

sentences.zh: 略舊識刁雙時為西河太守，略復歸之。

translations.literal: Lüe's old acquaintance Diao Shuang was then Western River Governor; Lüe again went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lüe's friend Diao Shuang was Western River governor; Lüe went to him next.

sentences.zh: 停止經年，雙乃令從子昌送略潛遁江左。

translations.literal: He stopped more than a year; Shuang then ordered his nephew Chang to send Lüe in secret to slip south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed a year; Shuang's nephew Chang smuggled him south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍甚禮敬之，封略為中山王，邑一千戶，宣城太守。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan treated him with great courtesy and respect; he enfeoffed Lüe as Prince of Zhongshan with a household of one thousand and made him Xuancheng Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan honored him, made him Prince of Zhongshan with a thousand households, and Xuancheng governor.

sentences.zh: 俄而徐州刺史元法僧據城南叛，州內士庶皆為法僧擁逼。

translations.literal: Soon Xuzhou Inspector Yuan Faseng held the south of the city and rebelled; gentry and commoners within the province were all compelled by Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Faseng rebelled at Xuzhou and dragged the province with him.

sentences.zh: 衍乃以略為大都督，令詣彭城，接誘初附。

translations.literal: Yan then made Lüe Grand Commander and ordered him to Pengcheng to receive and entice those newly submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan made Lüe grand commander and sent him to Pengcheng to win new submits.

sentences.zh: 略至，屯於河南，為安樂王鑒所破，略唯數十騎入城。

translations.literal: When Lüe arrived he encamped south of the River; he was broken by Prince of Anle Jian and Lüe had only several tens of horse enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lüe camped south of the River; Prince Jian of Anle routed him, and only a few dozen horsemen reached the city.

sentences.zh: 衍尋遣其豫章王綜鎮徐州，徵略與法僧同還。

translations.literal: Yan soon sent his Prince of Yuzhang Zong to hold Xuzhou and summoned Lüe and Faseng to return together.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Prince Zong of Yuzhang to hold Xuzhou and recalled Lüe and Faseng.

sentences.zh: 略雖在江南，自以家禍，晨夜哭泣，身若居喪。

translations.literal: Though Lüe was in the southland, because of his family's calamity he wept morning and night, his body as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he wept day and night for his family's ruin, living as in mourning.

sentences.zh: 又惡法僧為人，與法僧言，未嘗一笑。

translations.literal: He also hated Faseng's character; in speaking with Faseng he never once smiled.
translations.idiomatic: He despised Faseng and never smiled in his presence.

sentences.zh: 衍復除略衡州刺史，未行。

translations.literal: Yan again appointed Lüe Hengzhou Inspector; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yan named him inspector of Hengzhou; he never went.

sentences.zh: 會綜以城歸國，綜長史江革、司馬祖暅、將士五千人悉見擒虜。

translations.literal: When Zong surrendered the city to the state, Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Yang, and five thousand soldiers and officers were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong turned the city over to Wei, his chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Yang, and five thousand troops were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 肅宗敕有司悉遣革等還南，因以徵略。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong ordered the authorities to send Ge and the others entirely back south, and thereby summon Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong ordered the court to return Ge and the rest to the south and to summon Lue home.

sentences.zh: 衍乃備禮遣之。

translations.literal: Yan then prepared full rites and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then sent him away with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 略之將還也，衍為置酒餞別，賜金銀百斤，衍之百官，悉送別江上，遣其右衞徐確率百餘人送至京師。

translations.literal: When Lue was about to return, Yan set out wine for a farewell feast, bestowed a hundred jin of gold and silver, and all of Yan's hundred officials escorted him to the riverbank; he sent his Right Guard Xu Que with more than a hundred men to escort him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Lue prepared to leave, Yan gave a farewell feast and a hundred jin of gold and silver; every Liang minister saw him off on the river, and Xu Que of the Right Guard led a hundred men to escort him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔光祿大夫刁雙境首勞問，又敕徐州賜絹布各一千匹。

translations.literal: An edict made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Diao Shuang go to the border to greet and inquire after him; another edict granted Xuzhou a thousand bolts each of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong sent Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Diao Shuang to the frontier to welcome him and ordered a thousand bolts each of silk and cloth for Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 除略侍中、義陽王，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Lue was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Yiyang with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was named attendant-in-ordinary and prince of Yiyang with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 還達石人驛亭，詔宗室、親黨、內外百官先相識者，聽迎之近郊。

translations.literal: On reaching Shiren post station, an edict allowed kinsmen of the imperial clan, relatives, and all inner and outer officials who knew him beforehand to go to the near suburbs to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At Shiren post station an edict let clan kin, relatives, and any courtier who already knew him meet him in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 賜帛三千匹，宅一區，粟五千石，奴婢三十人。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk, one residence, five thousand shi of grain, and thirty slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He received three thousand bolts of silk, a mansion, five thousand shi of grain, and thirty slaves.

sentences.zh: 其司馬始賓除給事中、領直後，栗法光本縣令，刁昌東平太守，刁雙西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His former marshal Shi Bin was made Supervising Attendant and led the Straight Rear; Li Faguang was made magistrate of his home county; Diao Chang was made Administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang was made Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His old marshal Shi Bin became supervising attendant and led the Straight Rear; Li Faguang became his home-county magistrate; Diao Chang became Dongping administrator; Diao Shuang became Western Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 其略所至，一餐一宿之處，無不霑賞。

translations.literal: Every place Lue had stayed even a single meal or a single night received rewards without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Every inn or house that had fed or lodged him even once was showered with gifts.

sentences.zh: 尋改封東平王，又拜車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司、領左衞將軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was changed to Prince of Dongping; he was also made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Commander of the Left Guard, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was re-created prince of Dongping and named general of chariots and cavalry, left grand master of splendid happiness, equal in honor to the three dukes, and commander of the left guard while keeping attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 又本官領國子祭酒，遷大將軍、尚書令。

translations.literal: He also retained his original office as Director of the National University and was transferred to Great General and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the national university directorship and was promoted to great general and director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: [4]靈太后甚寵任之，其見委信，殆與元徽相埒。

translations.literal: [4] The Empress Dowager Ling greatly favored and trusted him; the trust placed in him was nearly on a par with Yuan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Empress Dowager Ling doted on him; her trust in him nearly matched Yuan Hui's.

sentences.zh: 於時天下多事，軍國萬端，略守常自保，無他裨益，唯唯具臣而已。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had many troubles and military and state affairs were myriad; Lue kept to routine and protected himself, with no other benefit—only a compliant minister.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil and state and army affairs endless; Lue held to routine, looked after himself, and offered nothing beyond a yes-man's compliance.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮，略之姑夫，略素所輕忽，略又黨於鄭儼、徐紇，榮兼銜之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage, whom Lue had always slighted; Lue also sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He, and Rong harbored resentment on both counts.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was his uncle by marriage and a man he had long despised; Lue also backed Zheng Yan and Xu He, and Rong hated him twice over.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛也，見害於河陰。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong took Luoyang, Lue died in the Heyin massacre.

sentences.zh: 贈以本官，加太保、司空、徐州刺史，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given his former offices plus Grand Guardian, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title: Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his ranks and was added grand guardian, minister of works, and Xuzhou inspector, styled Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子景式，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingshi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingshi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，北廣平太守。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Administrator of Northern Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuding he governed Northern Guangping.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 略 弟 纂

translations.literal: Lue's younger brother Zuan
translations.idiomatic: Lue's younger brother Zuan

sentences.zh: （附子 子獻）

translations.literal: (Appended son: Zixian)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended son: Zixian)

sentences.zh: 略弟纂，字紹興，頗有將略。

translations.literal: Lue's younger brother Zuan, styled Shaoxing, had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Lue's younger brother Zuan, styled Shaoxing, showed real talent in war.

sentences.zh: 為司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: He was made Libationer of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as libationer of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 聞熙舉兵，因逃奔於鄴，至即見擒，與熙俱死。

translations.literal: On hearing that Xi had raised troops, he fled to Ye and was seized on arrival; he died together with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi rose in arms he fled to Ye, was seized at once, and died with him.

sentences.zh: 追封北平縣公，贈安北將軍、恒州刺史，改封高唐縣開國侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Beiping County, given in gift General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou, changed to Marquis Who Founded the State of Gaotang with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made duke of Beiping county and given general who pacifies the north and Hengzhou inspector, then re-created founding marquis of Gaotang with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 子子獻，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zixian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒於涇州司馬。

translations.literal: He died as Vice Director of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Jingzhou vice director.

sentences.zh: 熙 異母弟 武邑王義興

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother by a different mother, Prince of Wuyi Yixing
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger half-brother, Prince of Wuyi Yixing

sentences.zh: （附子 述）

translations.literal: (Appended son: Shu)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended son: Shu)

sentences.zh: 熙異母弟義興，出後叔父並洛。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother by a different mother, Yixing, was given in adoption to his paternal uncle Bingluo.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's half-brother Yixing was adopted by their uncle Bingluo.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Outer Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign he was made outer attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 及熙之遇害也，義興以別後，故得不坐。

translations.literal: When Xi met disaster, Yixing, because he had been given out in adoption, was therefore not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was destroyed, Yixing escaped punishment because he had been adopted away.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who assists the state and regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he died at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈中軍將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General of the Central Army and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was named general of the central army and Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 後贈散騎常侍、征東將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service and General Who Pacifies the East; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was also given regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service and general who pacifies the east; other ranks unchanged.

sentences.zh: 義興妻，趙郡李氏。

translations.literal: Yixing's wife was Lady Li of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing's wife was Lady Li of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 李頗有婦工，為尒朱榮妻所親昵。

translations.literal: Li was skilled in women's crafts and was intimate with Erzhu Rong's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was skilled in women's crafts and close to Erzhu Rong's wife.

sentences.zh: 永安中，追封義興燕郡王，邑五百戶，尋改封鉅鹿王，又改封武邑王。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era Yixing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery with a fief of five hundred households; soon changed to Prince of Julu, then again to Prince of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an Yixing was posthumously made prince of Yan commandery with five hundred households, then prince of Julu, then prince of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 子述，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天平中，通直郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianping he was regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 扶風王怡

translations.literal: Prince of Fufeng Yi
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fufeng Yi

sentences.zh: 英弟怡，起家步兵校尉，轉城門校尉，遷鄯善鎮將。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Yi began as Commandant of Footsoldiers, transferred to Commandant of the City Gates, and was made General of Shanshan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yi rose from footsoldier commandant to city-gate commandant and then Shanshan garrison general.

sentences.zh: 所在貪暴，為有司所糾，逃竄得免。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was greedy and violent; the authorities impeached him, but he fled and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Every post found him greedy and brutal; impeached, he fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yan chang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Yanchang era.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，以尒朱榮婦兄，超贈驃騎大將軍、太尉公、雍州刺史、扶風王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's brother-in-law, he was posthumously promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Duke, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Prince of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign, as Erzhu Rong's brother-in-law, he was posthumously raised to general of agile cavalry, grand duke, Yongzhou inspector, and prince of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 子 魯郡王肅

translations.literal: Son: Prince of Lu Su
translations.idiomatic: Son: Prince of Lu Su

sentences.zh: （附子 道與）

translations.literal: (Appended son: Daoyu)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended son: Daoyu)

sentences.zh: 子道與，襲。

translations.literal: His son Daoyu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 除前將軍。

translations.literal: He was made General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general of the van.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 東海王曄

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Ye
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Donghai Ye

sentences.zh: 曄字華興，小字盆子。

translations.literal: Ye, styled Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.

sentences.zh: 性輕躁，有膂力。

translations.literal: By nature he was frivolous and rash, with great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was frivolous and rash, with uncommon strength.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎，稍遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He began as Secretary, and was gradually transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the secretariat and rose to regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封長廣王，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changguang with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he was made prince of Changguang with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 出為太原太守，行并州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Taiyuan and acted as commissioner for Bingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Taiyuan administrator and acting Bingzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，世隆等奔還并州，與尒朱兆會於建興，乃推曄為主，大赦所部，號年建明。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others fled back to Bingzhou, met Erzhu Zhao at Jianxing, and there set up Ye as ruler, proclaimed a general amnesty in their territory, and took the reign title Jianming.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death Shilong fled to Bingzhou, joined Erzhu Zhao at Jianxing, set Ye on the throne, amnestied their command, and declared the Jianming era.

sentences.zh: 尋為世隆等所廢。

translations.literal: Soon he was deposed by Shilong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shilong and his party deposed him.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝立，封曄為東海王，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Ye was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the former deposed emperor took the throne, Ye was made prince of Donghai with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，坐事賜死於第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign, for an offense he was granted death in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Deposed Emperor's reign he was sentenced to death in his own house.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir and the fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 城陽康王長壽

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Chengyang Changshou
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang of Chengyang Changshou

sentences.zh: 城陽王長壽，皇興二年封，拜征西大將軍、外都大官。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and made General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Director of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou was enfeoffed prince of Chengyang in Huangxing year 2 and named general who pacifies the west and grand director of the outer court.

sentences.zh: 出為沃野鎮都大將。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand General of Woye Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand general of Woye garrison.

sentences.zh: 性聰惠，善撫接，在鎮甚有威名。

translations.literal: By nature he was clever and skilled at winning people; at his post he had great prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and skilled at winning men, he held great authority in his command.

sentences.zh: 延興五年薨，諡康王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxing he died; posthumous title: Prince Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanxing year 5 and was posthumously styled Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子 多侯

translations.literal: Eldest son: Duohou
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son: Duohou

sentences.zh: 長子多侯，早卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Duohou died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Duohou died young.

sentences.zh: 次子 城陽懷王鸞

translations.literal: Second son: Prince Huai of Chengyang Luan
translations.idiomatic: Second son: Prince Huai of Chengyang Luan

sentences.zh: 次子鸞，字宣明。

translations.literal: The second son Luan, styled Xuanming.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Luan, styled Xuanming.

sentences.zh: 始繼叔章武敬王，及兄卒，還襲父爵。

translations.literal: At first he succeeded his uncle, Prince Jing of Zhangwu; when his elder brother died he returned to inherit his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He first succeeded his uncle, Prince Jing of Zhangwu; when his brother died he returned to his father's fief.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，以武藝著稱。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall, his belt ten wei around; he was famed for martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, with a ten-wei belt, he was famed for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 頻為北都大將。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he was made Grand General of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly named grand general of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: [5]高祖時，拜外都大官，又出為持節、都督河西諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護西戎校尉、涼州鎮都大將。

translations.literal: [5] In Gaozu's time he was made Grand Director of the Outer Court, then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Hexi, General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent Protector of the Western Rong, and Grand General of Liangzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Under Gaozu he became grand director of the outer court, then bearer of the staff, commander of Hexi, general who pacifies the west, protector of the western Rong, and Liangzhou garrison grand general.

sentences.zh: 改鎮立州，以鸞為涼州刺史，姑臧鎮都大將，餘如故。

translations.literal: The garrison was changed to establish a province; Luan was made Inspector of Liangzhou and Grand General of Guzang Garrison; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison became a province; Luan was made Liangzhou inspector and Guzang garrison grand general, other ranks unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後朝于京師。

translations.literal: Later he came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came to court.

sentences.zh: 會車駕南討，領鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, he was made General Who Stabilizes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, he was named general who stabilizes the army.

sentences.zh: 定都洛陽，高祖幸鄴，詔鸞留守。

translations.literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Gaozu visited Ye and ordered Luan to remain on guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was set at Luoyang, Gaozu went to Ye and left Luan to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 乃開建五等，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Then the five ranks of enfeoffment were established; his fief was a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted his fief stood at a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除使持節，征南大將軍，都督豫荊郢三州、河內山陽東郡諸軍事，與安南將軍盧淵、李佐攻赭陽，不克，敗退而還。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Commander of military affairs in Yu, Jing, and Ying provinces and in Henei, Shanyang, and Dong commanderies; with General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan and Li Zuo he attacked Zheyang, failed to take it, was defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He was bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the south, and commander of Yu, Jing, and Ying and of Henei, Shanyang, and Dong; with Lu Yuan and Li Zuo he attacked Zheyang, failed, and retreated beaten.

sentences.zh: 時高祖幸瑕丘，鸞請罪行宮。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was at Xiaqiu; Luan requested to come to the traveling palace to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then at Xiaqiu; Luan asked to come to the field palace and accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 高祖引見鸞等，責之曰：「卿等總率戎徒，義應奮節，而進不能夷拔賊城，退不能殄茲小寇，虧損王威，罪應大辟。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned Luan and the others and reproached them, saying: "You lead troops in mass; by right you should exert your utmost loyalty, yet advancing you could not storm the rebel city, retreating you could not destroy this petty bandit—you have diminished royal majesty and the crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received Luan and the rest and rebuked them: "You commanded armies and owed the utmost loyalty; yet you could neither take the rebel city nor crush this petty foe—you have shamed the throne and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 朕革變之始，事從寬貸，今捨卿等死罪，城陽降為定襄縣王，削戶五百。

translations.literal: At the beginning of my reform I act from leniency; now I spare you death; Prince of Chengyang is reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County with five hundred households cut from the fief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of my reforms I show mercy; I spare your lives; the prince of Chengyang is reduced to prince of Dingxiang county and loses five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 古者，軍行必載廟社之主，所以示其威惠各有攸歸，今徵卿等敗軍之罪於社主之前，以彰厥咎。

translations.literal: In antiquity, on campaign one carried the spirit-tablets of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain to show that authority and favor each had their proper place; now I summon your crime of the defeated army before the spirit-tablets to make your guilt manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity required temple tablets and altar spirits on campaign to show where authority and mercy lay; I now call your defeat before those spirits to expose your fault.

sentences.zh: 」後以留守之功，還復本封，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: " Later, for his merit in remaining on guard, his original fief was restored and two hundred households were added.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, for holding the capital, his original title was restored and two hundred households added.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍、河內太守，轉并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Administrator of Henei, then transferred to Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who overcomes the enemy and Henei administrator, then Bingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除平東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he became general who pacifies the east and Qingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 後轉安北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general who pacifies the north and Dingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 鸞愛樂佛道，修持五戒，不飲酒食肉，積歲長齋。

translations.literal: Luan loved and delighted in Buddhism and the Way; he kept the five precepts, did not drink wine or eat meat, and for years observed long fasts.
translations.idiomatic: Luan loved Buddhism; he kept the five precepts, ate no meat and drank no wine, and fasted for years.

sentences.zh: 繕起佛寺，勸率百姓，共為土木之勞，公私費擾，頗為民患。

translations.literal: He built Buddhist temples, urged the common people, and together imposed labor in earth and timber—public and private expenses were disturbed, and he became a real affliction to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He raised temples, pressed the people into earth-and-timber labor, and harassed public and private purse alike until he was a plague on the land.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞而詔曰：「鸞親唯宗懿，作牧大州，民物殷繁，綏寧所屬，宜克己厲誠，崇清樹惠，而乃驟相徵發，專為煩擾，編戶嗷嗷，家懷嗟怨。

translations.literal: When Shizong heard of it he issued an edict saying: "Luan is close kin of the imperial clan and governs a great province where the people are numerous; keeping the people at peace is his charge—he ought to restrain himself and show sincere devotion, honor purity and plant kindness, yet he has repeatedly called up labor and devoted himself solely to harassment; registered households cry out and every family harbors lament.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong heard and edicted: "Luan is imperial kin governing a populous province; his charge is peace, yet he has repeatedly conscripted labor for temples alone; households wail and every family grieves.

sentences.zh: 北州土廣，姦亂是由，準法尋愆，應加肅黜。

translations.literal: The northern provinces are broad in territory and disorder springs from this; by the law his faults should be found and he should be sternly removed.
translations.idiomatic: The north is vast and disorder breeds there; by law his faults warrant dismissal.

sentences.zh: 以鸞戚屬，情有未忍，可遣使者，以義督責，奪祿一周，微示威罰也。」

translations.literal: Because Luan is a kinsman, affection withholds full punishment; an envoy may be sent to reprove him in the name of righteousness, and his salary may be withheld for one cycle as a slight display of penalty."
translations.idiomatic: As kin, I spare him full disgrace; send an envoy to rebuke him and withhold one year's salary as a token punishment."

sentences.zh: 正始二年薨，時年三十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi he died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi year 2, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈帛六百匹，詔中書舍人王雲宣旨臨弔，贈鎮北將軍、冀州刺史，諡懷王。

translations.literal: Six hundred bolts of silk were granted in gift; an edict ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang Yun to proclaim the imperial message at the mourning; he was posthumously given General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Jizhou; posthumous title: Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred bolts of silk were granted; Wang Yun of the secretariat was sent to announce the throne's condolences; posthumously he was general who guards the north and Jizhou inspector, styled Huai.

sentences.zh: 子 城陽文獻王徽

translations.literal: Son: Prince Wenxian of Chengyang Hui
translations.idiomatic: Son: Prince Wenxian of Chengyang Hui

sentences.zh: （附子 延）

translations.literal: (Appended son: Yan)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended son: Yan)

sentences.zh: 子徽，字顯順。

translations.literal: His son Hui, styled Xianshun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, styled Xianshun.

sentences.zh: 粗涉書史，頗有吏才。

translations.literal: He had a rough acquaintance with books and histories and considerable talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: He had dipped into histories and showed real talent for office.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，襲封。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 除游擊將軍，出為河內太守。

translations.literal: He was made General of Raiding Cavalry and went out as Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general of raiding cavalry and Henei administrator.

sentences.zh: 在郡清整，有民譽。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was pure and orderly and had a reputation among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he ruled cleanly and won the people's praise.

sentences.zh: 徵拜長兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Acting Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as acting regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，除右將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time he was made General of the Right and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he became general of the right and Liangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 徽以徑途阻遠，固請不行。

translations.literal: Hui, because the route was long and obstructed, firmly requested not to go.
translations.idiomatic: The road to Liangzhou was long and hard; Hui begged off.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was made Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 其年，除後將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year he was made General of the Rear and Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was named general of the rear and Bingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是，州界夏霜，禾稼不熟，民庶逃散，安業者少。

translations.literal: Earlier, within the province's borders there had been summer frost; the grain did not ripen; the people fled and scattered, and few kept to their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier summer frost had struck the province, crops failed, people fled, and few could keep their fields.

sentences.zh: 徽輒開倉賑之，文武咸共諫止。

translations.literal: Hui at once opened the granaries to relieve them; civil and military officials alike remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui opened the granaries at once; civil and military officers alike tried to stop him.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「昔汲長孺，郡守耳，尚輒開倉，救民災弊，況我皇家親近，受委大藩，豈可拘法而不救民困也。

translations.literal: Hui said: "In the past Ji Changru, though only a commandery administrator, still opened the granaries to save the people from disaster and hardship—how much more I, close kin of the imperial house, entrusted with a great frontier, can I cling to the law and not rescue the people's distress?
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "Ji Changru was only a commandery chief yet opened the granaries in famine—how can a prince of the blood, entrusted with a great frontier, cling to statute and let the people starve?"

sentences.zh: 」先給後表。

translations.literal: " He distributed first and memorialized afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He gave grain first and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Suzong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong praised him.

sentences.zh: 加安北將軍。

translations.literal: He was added as General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 後拜安西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general who pacifies the west and Qinzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 詔書旦至夕發。

translations.literal: The edict arrived in the morning and he set out the same evening.
translations.idiomatic: The edict came at dawn and he left that evening.

sentences.zh: 徽以將之秦部，請詣闕恭授，仍表啟固陳，請不之職。

translations.literal: Hui, because he was about to go to the Qin region, requested to come to court to receive the appointment with ceremony and repeatedly memorialized, firmly asking not to take the post.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for Qin, he asked to receive the seal at court and memorialized again and again to decline the post.

sentences.zh: 改授輔國將軍，加度支尚書，進號鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to General Who Assists the State, added as Director of the Department of Revenue in the Masters of Writing, and advanced in title to General Who Stabilizes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to general who assists the state, made director of revenue in the masters of writing, and promoted to general who stabilizes the army.

sentences.zh: 于時，戎馬在郊，王師屢敗，徽以軍旅之費，上國封絹二千匹、粟一萬石以助軍用。

translations.literal: At that time war-horses were at the suburbs and the royal army had repeatedly been defeated; Hui, for military expenses, presented from his fief two thousand bolts of silk and ten thousand shi of grain to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: War had reached the suburbs and the royal army kept losing; Hui gave two thousand bolts of silk and ten thousand shi of grain from his fief for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 肅宗不納。

translations.literal: Suzong did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 又以本官兼吏部尚書，加侍中、征東將軍，遷衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrently Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, added as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the East, and transferred to General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He also held personnel in the masters of writing, attendant-in-ordinary, general who pacifies the east, then general of the guard and right grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左僕射，轉車騎將軍、儀同三司，固辭不拜，聽解侍中，然後受詔。

translations.literal: He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry with Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes; he firmly declined and would not accept; only after he was allowed to resign Attendant-in-Ordinary did he then accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice director of the masters of writing, then general of chariots and cavalry with equal honor to the three dukes; he refused until allowed to shed attendant-in-ordinary, then accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書令，加開府、西道行臺，不行。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Masters of Writing, added Opening of the Office and Western Circuit Touring Secretariat; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was director of the masters of writing with opening of the office and western touring secretariat, but would not take the field post.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后專制，朝綱頹褫。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Ling held sole power and court discipline collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ruled alone and court discipline rotted.

sentences.zh: 徽既居寵任，無所匡弼，與鄭儼之徒，更相阿黨。

translations.literal: Hui, though he held favored trust, offered no correction; with Zheng Yan and his sort he vied in forming factions.
translations.idiomatic: Though favored, Hui corrected nothing; he and Zheng Yan's circle traded factions.

sentences.zh: 外似柔謹，內多猜忌，睚眦之忿，必思報復。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed gentle and cautious; inwardly he was full of suspicion; the smallest grudge he was sure to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly mild, inwardly suspicious, he repaid every slight.

sentences.zh: 識者嫉之。

translations.literal: Men of insight despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing men despised him.

sentences.zh: 又不能防閑其妻于氏，遂與廣陽王淵姦通。

translations.literal: He also could not restrain his wife, the Lady Yu, who then had an affair with Prince Yuan of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He could not restrain his wife Lady Yu, who took Prince Yuan of Guangyang as lover.

sentences.zh: 及淵受任軍府，每有表啟，論徽罪過，雖涉誣毀，頗亦實焉。

translations.literal: When Yuan took command of the military headquarters, in every memorial he discussed Hui's faults; though it involved slander, much of it was true.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan commanded the army staff, every memorial denounced Hui; much of the slander was true.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐阼，拜司州牧，尋除司徒，仍領牧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Hui was made Governor of Sizhou; soon he was made Minister of Education while still holding the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang took the throne, Hui became Sizhou governor, then minister of education while keeping the governorship.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，徽從莊帝北巡，及車駕還宮，以與謀之功，除侍中、大司馬、太尉公，加羽葆、鼓吹，增邑通前二萬戶，餘官如故。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hui followed Emperor Xiaozhuang on the northern tour; when the imperial carriage returned to the palace, for his merit in the plot he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, Grand Duke, with feather canopy and martial music, and his fief was increased to twenty thousand households in all with the rest of his offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Hui followed Xiaozhuang north; on the return, for the plot's merit he was attendant-in-ordinary, grand marshal, and grand duke with canopy and martial music, his fief raised to twenty thousand households, other ranks unchanged.

sentences.zh: 徽表辭官封，前後屢上。

translations.literal: Hui memorialized to decline offices and fiefs, repeatedly submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized to decline rank and fief again and again.

sentences.zh: 又啟云：「河上之功，將士之力，求回所封，加諸勳義。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, saying: "The merit on the river was the soldiers' doing; I ask to return what was enfeoffed and add it to the meritorious."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The victory on the river belonged to the soldiers; return my fief to them."

sentences.zh: 」徽為莊帝親待，內懼榮寵，故有此辭，以防外議。

translations.literal: Hui was personally favored by Emperor Xiaozhuang; inwardly he feared excessive honor, and therefore made this declination to guard against outside criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang favored him; fearing excess honor, he declined to blunt gossip.

sentences.zh: 莊帝識其意，聽其辭封，不許讓官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang understood his intent and allowed him to decline the fief but did not permit him to yield the offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang saw through him, let the fief go, and kept the offices.

sentences.zh: 徽後妻，莊帝舅女。

translations.literal: Hui's later wife was the emperor's cousin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's second wife was the emperor's cousin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 侍中李彧，帝之姊婿。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 徽性佞媚，善自取容，挾內外之意，宗室親戚莫與比焉。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was fawning and ingratiating; he was skilled at winning favor for himself; relying on inside and outside connections, among the imperial clan and kin none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fawning and skilled at currying favor, he used court and clan ties as no other prince could match.

sentences.zh: 遂與彧等勸帝圖榮，莊帝亦先有意。

translations.literal: Then together with Yu and the others he urged the emperor to plot against Rong; Emperor Xiaozhuang too had long harbored the intent.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu and the rest he urged the emperor to move against Rong; Xiaozhuang had long meant to.

sentences.zh: 榮死，世隆等屯據不解。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shilong and the others held their positions and would not disband.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death Shilong's faction held together and would not disperse.

sentences.zh: 除徽太保，仍大司馬、宗師、錄尚書事，總統內外。

translations.literal: Hui was made Grand Guardian while still Grand Marshal, Imperial Clan Mentor, and Recorder of Affairs for the Masters of Writing, presiding over inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was made grand guardian while keeping grand marshal, imperial clan mentor, and recorder of the masters of writing, commanding court and camp.

sentences.zh: 徽本意謂榮死後，枝葉自應散亡。

translations.literal: Hui had originally supposed that after Rong's death the branches would naturally scatter and perish.
translations.idiomatic: He had assumed Rong's kin would scatter once Rong was dead.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱宗族，聚結謀難，徽算略無出，憂怖而已。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan gathered and plotted trouble, Hui's stratagems had no outcome—only fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan gathered to rebel, Hui had no plan—only fear.

sentences.zh: 性多嫉妬，不欲人居其前。

translations.literal: By nature he was full of jealousy and did not wish anyone to stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous by nature, he would brook no one ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 每入參謀議，獨與帝決。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered to discuss plans, he alone decided with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In council he alone decided with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有上軍國籌策者，並勸帝不納，乃云小賊何慮不除。

translations.literal: When court ministers submitted military and state strategy, he all urged the emperor not to accept it, saying petty bandits were nothing to worry about eliminating.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers offered strategy, he told the emperor to reject it, calling the Erzhu a trifle easily crushed.

sentences.zh: 又吝惜財用，自家及國。

translations.literal: He was also stingy with wealth, both for his household and for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was miserly with his own purse and the state's alike.

sentences.zh: 於是有所賞錫，咸出薄少，或多而中減，與而復追。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever there were rewards and gifts, they were all meager, or if large they were cut midway, or given and then pursued for return.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were always thin, or large gifts halved, or granted and then clawed back.

sentences.zh: 徒有糜費，恩不感物。

translations.literal: There was only waste in expenditure, and kindness did not move men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Money was wasted yet gratitude never followed.

sentences.zh: 莊帝雅自約狹，尤亦徽所贊成。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang by nature was himself frugal and narrow; Hui above all supported this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang was frugal by nature, and Hui above all encouraged it.

sentences.zh: 太府少卿李苗，徽司徒時司馬也，徽待之頗厚。

translations.literal: Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury Li Miao had been Hui's vice director when he was Minister of Education; Hui treated him quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao of the imperial treasury had been Hui's vice director when he was minister of education; Hui treated him well.

sentences.zh: 苗每致忠言，徽自得志，多不採納。

translations.literal: Miao often offered loyal words; once Hui had his wish, he mostly did not adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: Miao often spoke plainly; once Hui had power, he seldom listened.

sentences.zh: 苗謂人曰：「城陽本自蜂目，而豺聲復將露也。」

translations.literal: Miao said to others: "The Prince of Chengyang was born with bee eyes—and now the jackal's voice is about to show."
translations.idiomatic: Miao told others: "The prince of Chengyang was born with bee eyes—and now the jackal's howl is coming."

sentences.zh: 及尒朱兆之入，禁衞奔散，莊帝步出雲龍門。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered the city, the palace guards fled in disorder; Emperor Xiaozhuang walked out through the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang the guards broke; Xiaozhuang walked out the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 徽乘馬奔度，帝頻呼之，徽不顧而去。

translations.literal: Hui mounted his horse and galloped across; the emperor repeatedly called to him, but Hui paid no heed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hui spurred his horse across; the emperor called again and again, but Hui would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 遂走山南，至故吏寇彌宅。

translations.literal: He then fled south of the mountains to the house of his former clerk Kou Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He fled south of the mountains to his old clerk Kou Mi's house.

sentences.zh: 彌外雖容納，內不自安，乃怖徽云，官捕將至，令其避他所。

translations.literal: Mi outwardly received him but inwardly was ill at ease; he frightened Hui, saying officials were coming to seize him, and told him to hide elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sheltered him outwardly but inwardly feared him; he terrified Hui with word that arrest was near and sent him elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 使人於路邀害，送屍於尒朱兆。

translations.literal: He had men waylay and kill him on the road and sent the corpse to Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He had men ambush and kill him on the road and sent the body to Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，贈使持節、侍中、太師、大司馬、錄尚書事、司州牧，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, Recorder of Affairs for the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Sizhou; posthumous title: Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary, grand preceptor, grand marshal, recorder of the masters of writing, and Sizhou governor, styled Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 子延，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定末，官至太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he reached the post of Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuding he rose to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 徽 長兄 顯魏

translations.literal: Hui's elder brother: Xianwei
translations.idiomatic: Hui's elder brother: Xianwei

sentences.zh: 徽兄顯魏，給事中、司徒掾。

translations.literal: Hui's elder brother Xianwei was Supervising Attendant and Aide of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's elder brother Xianwei was supervising attendant and aide of the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously general who assists the state and Eastern Yuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 徽 次兄 顯恭

translations.literal: Hui's second elder brother: Xiangong
translations.idiomatic: Hui's second elder brother: Xiangong

sentences.zh: （附子 彦昭）

translations.literal: (Appended son: Yanzhao)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended son: Yanzhao)

sentences.zh: 徽次兄顯恭，字懷忠。

translations.literal: Hui's second elder brother Xiangong, styled Huaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's second elder brother Xiangong, styled Huaizhong.

sentences.zh: 揚州別駕，以軍功封平陽縣開國子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was Vice Director of Yangzhou; for military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis Who Founded the State of Pingyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yangzhou vice director and, for military merit, founding marquis of Pingyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除北中郎將，遷左將軍、東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made General of the North Center and transferred to General of the Left and Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou.
