translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he was general of the north center, then general of the left and Eastern Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 入為安東將軍、大司農卿。

translations.literal: He entered as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He came in as general who pacifies the east and grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 尋除中軍將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of the Central Army and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was general of the central army and Jingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 莊帝既殺尒朱榮，乃除顯恭使持節、都督晉建南汾三州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、兼尚書左僕射、西北道行臺、晉州刺史。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong, Xiangong was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Jin, Jian, and Nanfen provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Northwestern Circuit Touring Secretariat, and Inspector of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong, Xiangong was bearer of the staff, commander of Jin, Jian, and Nanfen, general who pacifies the west, left vice director of the masters of writing, northwestern touring secretariat, and Jinzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛後，死於晉陽。

translations.literal: After Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang he died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，贈衞大將軍、并州刺史，重贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given General of the Guard and Inspector of Bingzhou; later posthumously given again as General of Chariots and Cavalry with Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously general of the guard and Bingzhou inspector; later also general of chariots and cavalry with equal honor to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 子彥昭，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yanzhao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，漁陽太守。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Administrator of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuding he governed Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 顯恭 弟 襄城郡王旭

translations.literal: Xiangong's younger brother: Prince of Xiangcheng Xu
translations.idiomatic: Xiangong's younger brother: Prince of Xiangcheng Xu

sentences.zh: 顯恭弟旭，字顯和。

translations.literal: Xiangong's younger brother Xu, styled Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangong's younger brother Xu, styled Xianhe.

sentences.zh: 莊帝時，封襄城郡王，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangcheng commandery with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozhuang he was prince of Xiangcheng commandery with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武定末，位至大司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he reached the post of Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuding he rose to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 章武敬王太洛

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Zhangwu Tailuo
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Zhangwu Tailuo

sentences.zh: 章武王太洛，皇興二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in the second year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in Huangxing year 2.

sentences.zh: 追贈征北大將軍、章武郡王，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the North and Prince of Zhangwu commandery; posthumous title: Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was general who pacifies the north and prince of Zhangwu commandery, styled Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，以南安惠王第二子彬為後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the second son of Prince Hui of Nan'an, Bin, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign Bin, second son of Prince Hui of Nan'an, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 嗣子 彬

translations.literal: Heir: Bin
translations.idiomatic: Heir: Bin

sentences.zh: 彬，字豹兒，襲爵。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Bao'er, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Bao'er, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 勇健有武用。

translations.literal: Brave and strong, with martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and martial.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、都督東秦豳夏三州諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、西戎校尉、統萬鎮都大將、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Eastern Qin, Bin, and Xia provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Western Rong, Grand General of Tongwan Garrison, and Inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearer of the staff, commander of Eastern Qin, Bin, and Xia, general who pacifies the west, protector of the western Rong, Tongwan garrison grand general, and Shuozhou inspector.

sentences.zh: [6]以貪惏削封。

translations.literal: [6] For greed his fief was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Greed cost him part of his fief.

sentences.zh: 是時吐京胡反，詔彬持節，假平北將軍，行汾州事，率并肆之眾往討之，胡平，仍除征虜將軍、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the Tujing Hu rebelled; an edict made Bin Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the North, and Acting Commissioner for Bingzhou affairs; he led the forces of Bing and Si to attack them; when the Hu were pacified he was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing Hu rebelled, Bin was bearer of the staff, acting general who pacifies the north, and acting Fenzhou commissioner; he led Bing and Si troops to crush them, then was named general who punishes the barbarians and Fenzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 胡民去居等六百餘人，保險謀反，扇動徒類。

translations.literal: More than six hundred Hu households led by Quju and others held defiles and plotted rebellion, inciting their fellows.
translations.idiomatic: More than six hundred Hu households under Quju held the passes and stirred their clans to revolt.

sentences.zh: 彬請兵二萬，有司奏許之。

translations.literal: Bin requested twenty thousand troops; the authorities memorialized approval.
translations.idiomatic: Bin asked for twenty thousand men; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒曰：「何有動兵馬理也！

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly angered and said: "How can there be reason to move troops and horses!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu raged: "What reason is there to march an army!"

sentences.zh: 可隨宜肅治若不能權方靜帖，必須大眾者，則先斬刺史，然後發兵。

translations.literal: Deal with it as circumstances require; if you cannot by expedient means quiet and settle it, and a great force is truly needed, then first behead the inspector, and only then send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet them by whatever means fit; if you cannot settle it without a host, behead the inspector first, then raise the army.

sentences.zh: 」彬奉詔大懼，而率州兵，身先將士，討胡平之。

translations.literal: " Bin, receiving the edict, was greatly afraid; he then led the provincial troops, himself going before the soldiers, attacked the Hu, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Bin took the edict to heart and was terrified; he led the provincial troops in person at the head of his men, attacked the rebels, and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 太和二十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 23.

sentences.zh: 賜錢十萬、絹二百匹，贈以本官，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of silk, posthumously given his former office, and further made Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of silk, restored his former rank posthumously, and added Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 彬有五子。

translations.literal: Bin had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had five sons.

sentences.zh: 長子 章武莊武王融

translations.literal: Eldest son: Rong, Prince Zhuangwu of Zhangwu
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son: Rong, Prince Zhuangwu of Zhangwu

sentences.zh: （附子 景哲、朗、黃頭）

translations.literal: (With sons: Jingzhe, Lang, and Huangtou)
translations.idiomatic: (Sons: Jingzhe, Lang, and Huangtou)

sentences.zh: 長子融，字永興。

translations.literal: The eldest son Rong, style Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Rong, styled himself Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 儀貌壯麗，衣冠甚偉，性通率，有豪氣。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and splendid, his robes and cap very grand; by nature he was open and direct, with a bold spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in looks and splendid in dress; open by nature, with a bold spirit.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，拜祕書郎。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was made a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，復先爵，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign his father's enfeoffment was restored and he was made General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne his father's title was restored and he was named General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將，寇逼淮陽，梁城陷沒，詔融假節、征虜將軍、別將南討，大摧賊眾，還復梁城。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent generals to raid and press Huaiyang; Liang city fell. An edict made Rong acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and detached commander for the southern campaign; he greatly shattered the enemy host and recovered Liang city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Xiao Yan sent generals against Huaiyang and took Liang city. Rong was commissioned as acting commissioner and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians to lead the southern strike force; he broke the enemy badly and retook Liang city.

sentences.zh: 于時，揚州刺史元嵩為奴所害，敕融行揚州事。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Yang Province Yuan Song was killed by a slave; an edict ordered Rong to handle Yang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang inspector Yuan Song was murdered by a slave, Rong was ordered to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 尋除假節、征虜將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，兼司空，營陪景陵。

translations.literal: When Shizong died he was also made Minister of Works and oversaw construction at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's death he was named Minister of Works and supervised work at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 拜宗正卿，以本官行瀛州事，遇疾不行。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan, and with his former rank handled affairs of Ying Province; illness kept him from going.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the imperial clan and, retaining his rank, was to govern Ying—but illness kept him from setting out.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除散騎常侍、平東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Qing inspector.

sentences.zh: 還為祕書監，遷中護軍，進號撫軍將軍，領河南尹，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: He returned as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, moved to Central Guardian of the Army, advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, took charge as Intendant of Henan, and was further named General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: He came back as secretariat supervisor, became central guardian of the army, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, took Henan as intendant, and was further named General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 性尤貪殘，恣情聚斂，為中尉糾彈，削除官爵。

translations.literal: His nature was especially greedy and cruel; he indulged himself in amassing wealth. The commandant of justice impeached him and his rank and office were struck off.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and cruel by nature, he plundered at will until the commandant of justice impeached him and stripped rank and office.

sentences.zh: 汾夏山胡叛逆，連結正平、平陽，詔復融前封，征東將軍、持節、都督以討之。

translations.literal: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang. An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment, made him General Who Campaigns East, with staff and overall command, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain Hu in Fen and Xia rose, tying Zhengping to Pingyang. An edict restored Rong's title, named him General Who Campaigns East with staff and overall command, and sent him against them.

sentences.zh: 融寡於經略，為胡所敗。

translations.literal: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Rong lacked strategy and the Hu routed him.

sentences.zh: 久之，加散騎常侍、衞將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After a long while he was further made Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was again Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.

sentences.zh: 後賊帥鮮于脩禮寇暴瀛定二州，長孫稚等討之，失利。

translations.literal: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli ravaged Ying and Ding provinces; Zhangsun Zhi and others campaigned against him and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandit Xianyu Xiuli ravaged Ying and Ding; Zhangsun Zhi and others attacked him and lost.

sentences.zh: 除融車騎將軍，為前驅左軍都督，與廣陽王淵等共討脩禮。

translations.literal: Rong was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, forward commander of the Left Army, and with the Prince of Guangyang Yuan Yuan and others jointly attacked Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and forward commander of the left army; with Prince Yuan of Guangyang and others he marched against Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 師渡交津，葛榮殺脩禮而自立。

translations.literal: When the army crossed Jiaojin Ford, Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up as leader.
translations.idiomatic: As the host crossed Jiaojin Ford, Ge Rong killed Xiuli and took command himself.

sentences.zh: 轉營至白牛邏，輕騎擊融。

translations.literal: Shifting camp to the White Ox palisade, light cavalry struck Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's camp moved to the White Ox palisade, where light horse struck him.

sentences.zh: 融苦戰終日，更無外援，遂大奔敗，於陳見殺。

translations.literal: Rong fought bitterly all day; with no further outside aid he suffered a great rout and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rong fought all day without relief, was utterly broken, and fell in the field.

sentences.zh: 肅宗為舉哀於東堂，賜東園祕器、朝服一具、綵二千八百段，贈侍中、都督雍華岐三州諸軍事、本將軍、司空、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Suzong held mourning for him in the Eastern Hall, granted eastern-garden funeral gear, one set of court dress, and two thousand eight hundred lengths of colored silk, and posthumously made him Palace Attendant, overall commander of military affairs in Yong, Hua, and Qi provinces, with his former general's rank, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong mourned him in the Eastern Hall, granted state funeral gear, court dress, and twenty-eight hundred lengths of colored silk, and posthumously named him palace attendant, commander-in-chief over Yong, Hua, and Qi, with his former general's rank, Minister of Works, and Yong inspector.

sentences.zh: 尋以融死王事，進贈司徒，加前後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: Soon, because Rong died in the prince's service, he was further posthumously made Minister of Education, with front and rear guard music added.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because he had died in royal service, he was further posthumously made Minister of Education with full guard music before and behind.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊武。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Zhuangwu.

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu ordered the second son Yongquan of Hu'er's elder brother the Prince of Ruyin, Tiansi, to succeed him; he inherited the enfeoffment and later was renamed Siyu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu had Yongquan, second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince Tiansi of Ruyin, succeed the line; he inherited and was later renamed Siyu.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，蠕蠕犯塞，以思譽為鎮北大將軍、北征大都將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the Rouran raided the frontier; Siyu was made General Who Guards the North and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign, when the Rouran struck the border, Siyu was named General Who Guards the North and grand commander of the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 後除使持節、本將軍、領護匈奴校尉、都督、中軍都將。

translations.literal: Later he was made with full staff, with his former general's rank, Colonel Protecting the Xiongnu, overall commander, and Central Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held full staff, his former general's rank, the colonelcy protecting the Xiongnu, overall command, and the post of central army general.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、鎮東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將、營州刺史，加領護東夷校尉，轉為鎮北將軍，行鎮北大將軍。

translations.literal: He went out with full staff as General Who Guards the East, Grand Commander of the He-Long Garrison, and Inspector of Ying Province, further taking the colonelcy protecting the eastern barbarians; he was transferred to General Who Guards the North and acted as Grand General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: He went out with full staff as General Who Guards the East, grand commander of the He-Long garrison, and Ying inspector, also holding the colonelcy protecting the eastern Yi; he was then transferred to General Who Guards the North and acted as grand general guarding the north.

sentences.zh: 高祖引見百官於光極堂，謂思譽曰：「恒代路懸，舊都意重，故屈叔父遠臨此任，不可不敬慎所臨，以副朕望。

translations.literal: Gaozu received the hundred officials in the Hall of Luminous Pole and said to Siyu: "The road to Heng and Dai is remote; the old capital weighs on the heart—therefore I have bent my uncle to come far and take this post. You cannot but be reverent and cautious in what you oversee, to fulfill my hope.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received the officials in the Hall of Luminous Pole and told Siyu: "The road to Heng and Dai is long, and the old capital still weighs on the heart—so I have asked my uncle to come far and hold this post. Be reverent and careful in all you govern, and do not fail what I expect of you.

sentences.zh: 」及穆泰陰謀不軌，思譽知而不告，恕死，削封為庶人。

translations.literal: " When Mu Tai's secret plot went astray, Siyu knew but did not report it; he was pardoned from death and his enfeoffment was cut back to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: " When Mu Tai's plot came to light, Siyu had known but said nothing; he was spared execution but stripped to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 太和末，還復其王封。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taihe his princely title was restored.

translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi year 4.

translations.idiomatic: Xiu, Prince Jing of Anding

translations.literal: Prince of Anding Xiu was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing, appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, Prince of Anding, was enfeoffed in Huangxing year 2 and named General Who Campaigns South and grand master of the outer court.

sentences.zh: 休少而聰慧，治斷有稱。

translations.literal: Xiu was clever from youth and won praise for his judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from boyhood, Xiu was praised for his judgments.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，庫莫奚寇邊，以休為使持節、侍中、都督諸軍事、征東大將軍、領護東夷校尉、儀同三司、和龍鎮將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the Kumo Xi raided the border; Xiu was made with full staff, Palace Attendant, overall commander of military affairs, General Who Campaigns East, Colonel Protecting the Eastern Barbarians, with Three Precedents parity, and Commander of the He-Long Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu came to the throne and the Kumo Xi struck the border, Xiu was commissioned with full staff as palace attendant, overall commander, General Who Campaigns East, colonel protecting the eastern Yi, with Three Precedents parity, and commander of the He-Long garrison.

sentences.zh: 休撫防有方，賊乃款附。

translations.literal: Xiu's pacification and defense were well ordered; the bandits then submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu governed and defended with skill; the raiders then came over in good faith.

sentences.zh: 入為中都大官。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Master of the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as grand master of the central court.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕犯塞，出為使持節、征北大將軍、撫冥鎮大將。

translations.literal: When the Rouran raided the frontier he went out with full staff as General Who Campaigns North and Grand Commander of the Fuming Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran struck again he went out with full staff as General Who Campaigns North and grand commander of the Fuming garrison.

sentences.zh: 休身先將士，擊虜退之。

translations.literal: Xiu went before the soldiers in person and struck the barbarians, driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu led from the front, struck the barbarians, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 入為內都大官，遷太傅。

translations.literal: He entered as Grand Master of the Inner Court and was promoted Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He came in as grand master of the inner court and was promoted Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 及開建五等，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were newly established, his fief was two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were first set up, his fief stood at two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，領大司馬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he took charge as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he served as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 高祖親行諸軍，遇休以三盜人徇於六軍，將斬之，有詔赦之。

translations.literal: Gaozu personally led the armies; he encountered Xiu with three thieves paraded before the six armies, about to be executed, when an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was leading the armies in person when Xiu had three thieves displayed before the host and was about to execute them; an edict then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 休執曰：「陛下將遠清衡霍，故親御六師，跋涉野次，軍行始爾，已有姦竊，如其不斬，何以息盜，請必行刑，以肅姦慝。

translations.literal: Xiu held fast and said: "Your Majesty is about to go far and clear Heng and Huo; therefore you personally lead the six armies, tramping through the wilds. The march has only just begun and already there are thieves. If they are not beheaded, how can theft be stilled? I beg that the punishment be carried out without fail, to awe the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu pressed his case: "Your Majesty means to go far and clear Heng and Huo, and so leads the six armies yourself through the wilds. The march has barely begun and thieves already appear. If they are not beheaded, how will theft cease? I beg that the sentence be carried out, to awe the wicked.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「大司馬執憲，誠應如是。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The Grand Marshal holds the law—indeed it should be so.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne answered: "The Grand Marshal holds the law—so it should be.

sentences.zh: 但因緣會，朕聞王者之體，亦時有非常之澤，雖違軍法，可特原之。

translations.literal: But by chance of circumstance I have heard that the body of a king also at times grants an extraordinary grace; though it violates military law, they may be specially spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chance has put me here, and I have heard that a king's body may at times grant an extraordinary grace; though this breaks military law, let them be specially spared.

sentences.zh: 」休乃奉詔。

translations.literal: " Xiu then received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu then obeyed the edict.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂司徒馮誕曰：「大司馬嚴而秉法，諸軍不可不慎。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to the Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds to the law; the armies cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds the law—the armies had better take care.

sentences.zh: 」於是六軍肅然。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the six armies were in awe.
translations.idiomatic: " After that the six armies stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 定都洛邑，休從駕幸鄴。

translations.literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the imperial progress to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the court to Ye.

sentences.zh: 命休率從駕文武，迎家于平城。

translations.literal: He was ordered to lead the civil and military who followed the progress and bring the household from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead the civil and military of the progress and bring the household down from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖親餞休於漳水之北。

translations.literal: Gaozu personally saw Xiu off north of the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu personally saw him off north of the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 十八年，休寢疾，高祖幸其第，流涕問疾，中使醫藥，相望於路。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Xiu lay ill in bed; Gaozu visited his residence, wept and inquired after his illness, and palace envoys with medicine followed one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 Xiu took to his bed; Gaozu came to his house, wept, and asked after him, while palace envoys with medicine crowded the road.

sentences.zh: 薨，賵帛三千匹。

translations.literal: He died; funeral gifts were three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He died; funeral gifts were three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 自薨至殯，車駕三臨。

translations.literal: From death until the encoffining the imperial carriage came three times.
translations.idiomatic: From his death to encoffining the emperor came three times.

sentences.zh: 高祖至其門，改服錫衰，[10]素弁加絰。

translations.literal: Gaozu came to his gate, changed dress and granted hemp mourning, [10] plain cap with hemp band.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu came to his gate, changed into mourning dress and granted hemp, [10] with plain cap and hemp band.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、百官皆從行弔禮。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the hundred officials all followed in performing mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and all officials followed in the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，又贈布帛二千匹，諡曰靖王。

translations.literal: When the time came to bury, two thousand more bolts of silk were granted; posthumous title: Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At burial two thousand more bolts of silk were granted; posthumous title: Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 詔假黃鉞，加羽葆、鼓吹、虎賁、班劍六十三人，悉準三老尉元之儀。

translations.literal: An edict lent the yellow battle-axe, added feather canopy, guard music, tiger guards, and sixty-three sword-bearers of the imperial guard—all matching the rites for the Three Elders, Yuan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lent the yellow axe, with feather canopy, guard music, tiger guards, and sixty-three imperial sword-bearers—all matching the rites for the Three Elders Yuan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖親送出郊，慟哭而返，諸王恩禮莫比焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu personally escorted him beyond the suburbs, wept and returned, and no prince received such favor in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu escorted him beyond the suburbs, wept on his return, and no prince was ever mourned with such honor.

sentences.zh: 世宗世，配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he was given a place in the temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he was given a place in the ancestral temple.

translations.literal: Eldest son: An
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son: An

sentences.zh: 長子安，幼年早卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son An died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son An died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 次子 燮

translations.literal: Second son: Xie
translations.idiomatic: Second son: Xie

sentences.zh: 次子燮，除下大夫。

translations.literal: The second son Xie was made Lower Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Xie was made lower grand master.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，襲拜太中大夫，除征虜將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he inherited and was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he inherited and was made grand master of the palace, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Hua inspector.

sentences.zh: 燮表曰：「謹惟州治李潤堡，雖是少梁舊地，晉、芮錫壤，然胡夷內附，遂為戎落。

translations.literal: Xie memorialized, saying: "I respectfully consider the seat of Zhou prefecture at Li Run Fort: though it is the old ground of Lesser Liang and the fief-grant of Jin and Rui, yet with Hu and Yi submitting within, it has become a barbarian settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Xie submitted a memorial: "I have weighed the seat of Zhou prefecture at Li Run Fort. It lies on old Lesser Liang ground and on Jin and Rui's grant, but once the Hu and Yi came in it turned into a barbarian quarter.

sentences.zh: 城非舊邑先代之名，爰自國初，護羌小戍。

translations.literal: The city is not an old town's name of former generations; from the founding of the state it was a small garrison protecting the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The town bears no ancient name from earlier ages; from the dynasty's founding it was only a small garrison guarding the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 及改鎮立郡，依岳立州，因籍倉府，未刊名實。

translations.literal: When the garrison was changed to a commandery and a prefecture set up on the model of a mountain, the name and reality were never carved in the registers of the granary offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the post became a commandery and a prefecture was raised on a mountain model, name and fact were never fixed in the granary registers.

sentences.zh: 竊見馮翊古城，羌魏兩民之交，許洛水陸之際，先漢之左輔，皇魏之右翼，形勝名都，實惟西蕃奧府。

translations.literal: I see the old city of Fengyi: where the Qiang and Wei peoples meet, on the water and land route between Xu and Luo—a left-hand guard of Former Han, the right wing of august Wei, a stronghold and famous capital, truly the inner treasury of the western border.
translations.idiomatic: I look at the old city of Fengyi, where Qiang and Wei meet, on the water road between Xu and Luo—Former Han's left-hand guard, august Wei's right wing, a fortress and famous capital, truly the inner treasury of the western marches.

sentences.zh: 今州之所在，豈唯非舊，至乃居岡飲澗，井谷穢雜，昇降劬勞，往還數里。

translations.literal: Where the prefecture now sits is not only not the old site; it even dwells on hills and drinks from ravines, wells and valleys foul and mixed, climbing and descending toilsome, coming and going several li.
translations.idiomatic: Where the prefecture sits now is not merely off the old site; people live on ridges, drink from gullies, wells and lanes are foul and tangled, and every trip up or down costs miles of labor.

sentences.zh: 譐誻明昏，有虧禮教。

translations.literal: Noise and clamor from dawn to dusk injure ritual and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Noise from dawn to dusk mars ritual and teaching.

sentences.zh: 未若馮翊，面華渭，包原澤，井淺池平，樵牧饒廣。

translations.literal: It is not like Fengyi, facing Hua and Wei, embracing plains and marshes, with shallow wells and level pools, firewood and pasture ample.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi faces Hua and Wei, holds plains and marshes, has shallow wells and level pools, and ample wood and pasture.

sentences.zh: 採材華陰，陸運七十；

translations.literal: Timber is taken at Huayin; overland transport seventy li;
translations.idiomatic: Timber can be taken at Huayin and hauled overland seventy li;

sentences.zh: 伐木龍門，順流而下。

translations.literal: wood is cut at Longmen and floated downstream.
translations.idiomatic: wood can be cut at Longmen and floated downstream.

sentences.zh: 陪削舊雉，功省力易，人各為己，不以為勞。

translations.literal: Trimming the old ramparts saves labor and strength; each man works for himself and does not count it hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Trimming the old walls saves labor; each man works for himself and does not call it a burden.

sentences.zh: 昔宋民無井，穿井而忻得人；

translations.literal: In former times the people of Song had no wells; they dug a well and rejoiced to gain a man;
translations.idiomatic: Once the people of Song had no wells; they dug one and rejoiced to gain a man;

sentences.zh: 況合城無水，得水而不家慶。

translations.literal: how much more when a whole city had no water and, gaining water, would not celebrate in every household.
translations.idiomatic: how much more when a whole city lacked water—would not every household celebrate once water came?

sentences.zh: 竊聞前政刺史，非是無意，或值兵舉，或遇年災，緣此契闊，稽延至此。

translations.literal: I hear that former prefects were not without intent; sometimes troops were raised, sometimes years brought disaster—because of this the matter was left open and has been delayed until now.
translations.idiomatic: I hear earlier prefects were not without the idea; war or famine always intervened, so the plan was set aside and has waited until now.

sentences.zh: 去歲已熟，秋方大登，四境晏安，京師無事。

translations.literal: Last year the harvest was ripe; this autumn the great crop is coming in; the four borders are calm and the capital has no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's harvest was good; this autumn promises a great crop; the borders are quiet and the capital untroubled.

sentences.zh: 丁不十錢之費，人無八旬之勤。

translations.literal: Corvée costs less than ten cash per man; the people need no labor of eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée will cost less than ten cash a man; the people need no eighty-day levy.

sentences.zh: 損輕益重，乞垂昭鑒。

translations.literal: To lighten the small and weight the great—I beg that your clear sight grant this.
translations.idiomatic: A small cost for a great gain—I beg your clear sight to grant it.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔曰：「一勞永逸，便可聽移。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict said: "One effort for lasting ease—you may move as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne answered: "One effort for lasting ease—move as you propose.

sentences.zh: 」後除征虜將軍、豳州刺史。

translations.literal: " Later he was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Inspector of Bin Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Bin inspector.

sentences.zh: 延昌四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanzhang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanzhang year 4.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously given his former general's rank and made Inspector of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his general's rank and was made Shuo inspector.

sentences.zh: 子 超

translations.literal: Son: Chao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chao

sentences.zh: （附子 孝景）

translations.literal: (With son: Xiaojing)
translations.idiomatic: (Son: Xiaojing)

sentences.zh: 子超，字化生。

translations.literal: His son Chao, style Huasheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao styled himself Huasheng.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，襲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong came to the throne he inherited.

sentences.zh: 時以胡國珍封安定公，改封北平王。

translations.literal: At that time because Hu Guozhen was enfeoffed Duke of Anding, he was changed to Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hu Guozhen had been enfeoffed Duke of Anding, Chao was re-created Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 拜城門校尉、通直散騎常侍、東中郎將。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the City Gates, Regular Attendant in Direct Service, and General of the Eastern Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was made colonel of the city gates, regular attendant in direct service, and general of the eastern gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 尋除光祿大夫，領將作大匠。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and took charge as Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 後復本封。

translations.literal: Later his original enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his original title was restored.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之入洛，超避難洛南，遇寇見害。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled to the south of Luo and met bandits and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled south of the Luo and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: [11]莊帝初，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was posthumously made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, with Three Precedents parity, and Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: [11] When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was posthumously General of the Chariots and Cavalry with Three Precedents parity and Qi inspector.

sentences.zh: 子孝景，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiaojing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaojing inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，通直郎。

translations.literal: In Wuding he was Gentleman in Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding he was gentleman in direct service.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 燮 弟 願平

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother: Yuanping
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother: Yuanping

sentences.zh: 燮弟願平，清狂無行。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was unrestrained and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and without conduct.

sentences.zh: 高祖末，拜員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozu's reign he was appointed Outer Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Gaozu's reign he was made outer gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，遷給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was promoted Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he was promoted attendant.

sentences.zh: 悖惡日甚，殺人劫盜，公私成患。

translations.literal: His perversity and wickedness grew daily; he killed men and robbed and plundered, becoming a scourge to public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: His perversity deepened daily—murder, robbery, plunder—until he scourged public and private life alike.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其戚近，未忍致之於法，乃免官，禁之別館。

translations.literal: Shizong, because he was a close kinsman, could not bear to bring him under the law; he was dismissed from office and confined in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, as a near kinsman, could not bear to punish him by law; he was dismissed and shut in a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 館名愁思堂，冀其克念。

translations.literal: The lodge was named Hall of Sorrowful Thought, in hope that he would restrain his thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge was called the Hall of Sorrowful Thought, in hope he would check himself.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，願平乃得出。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, Yuanping was then able to come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, Yuanping was let out.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，以其暴亂不悛，詔曰：「願平志行輕疏，每乖憲典，可還於別館，依前禁錮。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because his violence and disorder did not mend, an edict said: "Yuanping's will and conduct are light and scattered; he constantly violates the statutes—he may be returned to the separate lodge and confined as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling ruled, his violence still unabated, an edict said: "Yuanping's will and conduct are loose; he constantly breaks the law—return him to the separate lodge and confine him as before.

sentences.zh: 」久之，解禁還家，付師嚴加誨奬。

translations.literal: " After a long while the confinement was lifted and he returned home, handed to tutors for strict admonition.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while the confinement was lifted; he went home under tutors who were to admonish him strictly.

sentences.zh: 後拜通直散騎常侍、前將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Service and Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was regular attendant in direct service and forward general.

sentences.zh: 坐裸其妻王氏於其男女之前，又強姦妻妹於妻母之側。

translations.literal: He was convicted of stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before her sons and daughters, and of forcing himself on his wife's younger sister before his wife's mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before their children and of forcing his wife's younger sister before his mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞侯剛案以不道，處死，絞刑，會赦免，黜為員外常侍。

translations.literal: The Imperial Censor Hou Gang judged it unnatural conduct and sentenced him to death by strangulation; an amnesty spared him; he was demoted to Outer Attendant in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor Hou Gang tried him for unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation; an amnesty spared him and he was demoted to outer attendant in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，卒。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 子 緒

translations.literal: Son: Xu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xu

sentences.zh: （附子 南郡王長春）

translations.literal: (With son: Changchun, Prince of Nanjun)
translations.idiomatic: (Son: Changchun, Prince of Nanjun)

sentences.zh: 子緒，幽州安西府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xu, Recorder in the Anxi Office of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu was recorder in the Anxi office of You Province.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，直閤將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was direct attendant general.

sentences.zh: 尋為持節、兼武衞將軍、關右慰勞十二州大使，遂沒吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Soon he was made with staff, acting Martial Guard General, and envoy comforting the twelve provinces west of the Pass; he then fell among the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was commissioned with staff as acting martial guard general and envoy comforting the twelve provinces west of the Pass; he then perished among the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 子長春，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Changchun, Outer Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changchun was outer attendant at the palace secretariat in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 武定初，封南郡王，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was created Prince of Nanjun with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 願平 弟 永平

translations.literal: Yuanping's younger brother: Yongping
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping's younger brother: Yongping

sentences.zh: 願平弟永平，征虜將軍、南州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanping's younger brother Yongping, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Inspector of Nan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping's younger brother Yongping was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Nan inspector.

sentences.zh: [12]為城民華延明所害。

translations.literal: [12] He was killed by the city man Hua Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: [12] He was killed by a townsman, Hua Yanming.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，追贈使持節、侍中、都督定瀛幽三州諸軍事、衞將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given full staff, Palace Attendant, overall command of military affairs in Ding, Ying, and You provinces, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously given full staff, palace attendant, overall command in Ding, Ying, and You, General of the Guard, and Ding inspector.

sentences.zh: 永平 弟 珍平

translations.literal: Yongping's younger brother: Zhenping
translations.idiomatic: Yongping's younger brother: Zhenping

sentences.zh: 永平弟珍平，司州治中。

translations.literal: Yongping's younger brother Zhenping, Chief Clerk of Zhou Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping's younger brother Zhenping was chief clerk of Zhou Province.

sentences.zh: 子 叔遵

translations.literal: Son: Shuzun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shuzun

sentences.zh: 子叔遵，員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Shuzun, Outer Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in Ordinary Service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuzun was outer attendant at the palace secretariat in ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 珍平 弟 貴平

translations.literal: Zhenping's younger brother: Guiping
translations.idiomatic: Zhenping's younger brother: Guiping

sentences.zh: 珍平弟貴平，羽林監、轉射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Zhenping's younger brother Guiping, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, then Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenping's younger brother Guiping was supervisor of the feathered forest, then colonel of the archers who shoot by sound.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，除散騎常侍、宗正少卿，封東萊王，邑百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was made Regular Attendant and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed Prince of Donglai with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was regular attendant and vice director of the imperial clan, created Prince of Donglai with one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除平北將軍、南相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Nanxiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the North and Nanxiang inspector.

sentences.zh: 莊帝既殺尒朱榮，加武衞將軍，兼侍中，為河北、山東慰勞大使。

translations.literal: After Zhuangdi had killed Erzhu Rong he was further made Martial Guard General and concurrent Palace Attendant, and made envoy comforting Hebei and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangdi killed Erzhu Rong he was further martial guard general and concurrent palace attendant, and envoy comforting Hebei and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 至定州東北，為幽州大都督侯淵所執，送於晉陽。

translations.literal: Reaching the northeast of Ding Province, he was seized by the Grand Commander of You Province Hou Yuan and sent to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near northeast Ding he was seized by You grand commander Hou Yuan and sent to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 後還洛。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，以本官行青州事，屬土民崔祖螭作逆，賊徒甚盛，圍逼東陽一百餘日。

translations.literal: In the time of the Former Deposed Emperor he held his former rank and handled affairs of Qing Province; the local man Cui Zuchi rebelled, the rebel band very strong, besieging Dongyang for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor he governed Qing with his former rank; the local strongman Cui Zuchi rebelled, his host was large, and Dongyang was besieged for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 貴平率城民固守，又令將士開門交戰。

translations.literal: Guiping led the townspeople in a firm defense and also ordered officers and soldiers to open the gates and give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guiping led the townspeople in a stubborn defense and ordered his officers to open the gates and fight.

sentences.zh: 大軍救至，遂擒祖螭等，斬之。

translations.literal: When the great army arrived in relief, Zuchi and the others were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When relief arrived, Zuchi and his fellows were taken and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 還，除車騎將軍，加散騎常侍，遷左衞將軍、宗師，又遷車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: On his return he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, further Regular Attendant, promoted Left Guard General and Director of the Imperial Clan, then promoted General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, and Three Precedents parity.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was General of the Chariots and Cavalry with added regular attendant, then left guard general and director of the imperial clan, then again General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, with Three Precedents parity.

sentences.zh: 貴平人才險薄，為出帝所信。

translations.literal: Guiping's talent was treacherous and shallow; he was trusted by the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guiping was gifted but mean-spirited and thin-skinned, and the Deposed Emperor placed his faith in him.

sentences.zh: 出為青州刺史，又加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，為幽州大都督侯淵所害。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Qing Province; was further made General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Guardian, and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with ritual parity to the Three Excellencies; and was killed by Hou Yuan, Grand Commander of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Qing inspector, he was also named general of agile cavalry, grand guardian, and bearer of the golden halberd with ritual parity to the three excellencies, then slain by Hou Yuan, grand commander of You.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：南安原始要終，善不掩惡。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Nan'an traced from origin to end; good does not cover evil.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: For the Nan'an line, from first to last, merit never hid fault.

sentences.zh: 英將帥之用，有聲於時。

translations.literal: Ying's use as a commander had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's career as a field commander won him a name among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 熙、略兄弟，早播民譽，或才疏志大，或器狹任廣，咸不能就其功名，俱至非命，惜也。

translations.literal: The brothers Xi and Lue early spread popular renown; one had talent sparse and ambition great, one had capacity narrow and charge broad—none could complete their fame and merit; all met untimely deaths—a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Lue won public praise early; one aimed too high for his gifts, the other took too wide a brief for his narrow talents—neither finished his career, and both died before their time. A loss.

sentences.zh: 康王不永，鸞起家聲。

translations.literal: Prince Kang did not live long; Luan rose to a household name.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang died young; Luan built the family's later fame.

sentences.zh: 徽飾智矯情，外諂內忌，永安之禍，誰任其責？

translations.literal: Hui adorned wisdom and feigned feeling, fawning without and jealous within; the Yong'an calamity—who bears the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Hui dressed up cleverness and played at feeling, servile outwardly and envious within; for the Yong'an disaster, who should answer?

sentences.zh: 宛其死也，固其宜哉。

translations.literal: Yuanping's death—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: That Yuanping should die as he did was only just.

sentences.zh: 章武、樂陵，蓋不足數。

translations.literal: Zhangwu and Leling—hardly worth counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu and Leling scarcely merit mention.

sentences.zh: 靖王聰斷威重，見稱太和，美矣。

translations.literal: Prince Jing was sharp, decisive, and august; praised in the Taihe era—admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing was keen, firm, and commanding, and won praise in the Taihe years—a fine record.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 亦或居安生疾 諸本「安」訛「要」。

translations.literal: Or perhaps in ease one breeds illness. In various editions "an" (ease) is written erroneously as "yao" (want).
translations.idiomatic: "Or perhaps ease breeds illness": editions corrupt an (ease) to yao (want).

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 8, Annals of Shizong, Zhengshi year 3, ninth month, day jichou, records this event and also has "Right Vice Director Liu Yan."

sentences.zh: 柳惔為右僕射見梁書卷二武帝紀天監三年正月戊申條及卷一二本傳。

translations.literal: Liu Yan as Right Vice Director appears in Liang shu juan 2, Annals of Emperor Wu, first month, day wushen of Tianjian year 3, and in juan 12, his basic biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan's tenure as right vice director is attested in Liang shu juan 2 (Wu annals, Tianjian 3.1 wushen) and juan 12 (his biography).

sentences.zh: 「左」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "left" is erroneous; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The character "left" is corrupt; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 一一具聞 諸本「一一」二字訛作「三」，不可通，局本改作「王」。

translations.literal: One by one fully reported. In various editions the two characters "one by one" are erroneously written as "three," which will not parse; the Bureau edition changes them to "Wang."
translations.idiomatic: "One by one fully reported": editions corrupt the binome "one by one" to "three," which will not parse; the Bureau text reads "Wang."

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing. Commentary: Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Lue
translations.idiomatic: "Transferred to grand general and director of the Masters of Writing": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Lue

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一三九〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 139〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 139

sentences.zh: 稱「尋遷驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，加國子祭酒，俄涉尚書令」。

translations.literal: It says: "Soon transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Golden Halberd with ritual parity to the Three Excellencies, added as Chancellor of the Imperial University; shortly after he took up Director of the Masters of Writing."
translations.idiomatic: reads: "Soon made general of agile cavalry and bearer of the golden halberd with ritual parity to the three excellencies, with the added post of chancellor of the imperial university; shortly thereafter he became director of the Masters of Writing."

sentences.zh: 北魏大將軍在三公上，元略軍號本是車騎大將軍，一般不可能超遷大將軍。

translations.literal: In Northern Wei the rank of Grand General stood above the Three Excellencies; Yuan Lue's military title was originally General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Wei, grand general outranked the three excellencies; Yuan Lue's army title had been general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 這裏「大將軍」上當脫「驃騎」二字。

translations.literal: Here above "Grand General" the two characters "Agile Cavalry" must have dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: Here the two characters "agile cavalry" must have dropped before "grand general."

sentences.zh: 頻為北都大將 按「北」下疑脫「鎮」字。

translations.literal: Repeatedly served as Grand General of the Northern Capital. Commentary: Below "bei" (north) a character "zhen" (garrison) is probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: "Repeatedly grand general of the northern capital": the character zhen (garrison) is probably missing after bei (north).

translations.idiomatic: "Commander-in-chief of Tongwan garrison and inspector of Shuozhou": Zhang Senkai says, "Bei shi

translations.literal: 〈juan 18〉
translations.idiomatic: juan 18

translations.literal: has "Shuo" written as "Xia."
translations.idiomatic: reads Shuo as Xia."

sentences.zh: 據上文「為統萬鎮都大將」，統萬在夏州，不在朔州，疑魏書誤。

translations.literal: According to the text above, "served as Commander-in-Chief of Tongwan Garrison"—Tongwan lies in Xia Province, not Shuozhou; the Wei shu is probably in error.
translations.idiomatic: The line above makes him commander-in-chief of Tongwan garrison; Tongwan lay in Xia, not Shuo—Wei shu is likely wrong.

sentences.zh: 又刺史例不在所督州之外，上文『都督東秦豳夏三州』，無朔州，尤確證也。

translations.literal: Moreover, by precedent an inspector was not posted outside the province he commanded; above it says "commanded Dong, Qin, and Xia—three provinces," with no Shuozhou—a still stronger proof.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, inspectors were not usually posted outside the provinces they commanded; above he "commanded Dong, Qin, and Xia"—with no Shuo—which clinches the point.

translations.idiomatic: also has "commander-in-chief of Tongwan-Tu garrison and inspector of Xia"; Zhang is right.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書左司郎中 墓誌集釋元湛墓誌

translations.literal: Transferred to Langzhong of the Left Bureau of the Masters of Writing. Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Zhan
translations.idiomatic: "Transferred to langzhong of the left bureau of the Masters of Writing": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Zhan

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一五二〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 152〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 152

sentences.zh: 作「尋補尚書左士郎中」。

translations.literal: It reads "Soon appointed Langzhong of the Left Scholar Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: reads: "Soon appointed langzhong of the left scholar bureau."

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷二四職官志尚書郎條稱西晉時尚書有三十五曹，其中有「左、右士」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Jin shu juan 24, Monograph on Offices, entry for Masters of Writing Lang, states that in Western Jin the Masters of Writing had thirty-five bureaus, among them "Left and Right Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Jin shu juan 24 (offices monograph), Masters of Writing lang entry, lists thirty-five Western Jin bureaus, including "left and right scholar."

sentences.zh: 又稱東晉所省尚書諸曹中也有「左、右士」。

translations.literal: It also states that among the Masters of Writing bureaus reduced in Eastern Jin there were also "Left and Right Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: The same passage notes that Eastern Jin's reductions still retained "left and right scholar" among the Masters of Writing bureaus.

sentences.zh: 知左、右士曹是西晉舊置。

translations.literal: Thus the Left and Right Scholar bureaus were an old Western Jin establishment.
translations.idiomatic: So the left and right scholar bureaus were a Western Jin foundation.

sentences.zh: 本書卷八一山偉傳

translations.literal: This book, juan 81, Biography of Shan Wei
translations.idiomatic: This book, juan 81, biography of Shan Wei

translations.literal: 〈supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: supplement

sentences.zh: 說山偉「後正名士郎」，「名」字當是「左」或「右」之訛，可證北魏有左、右士郎中。

translations.literal: says that Shan Wei "later was regularized as Lang of the Famous Scholars"; the character "ming" (famous) must be a corruption of "zuo" (left) or "you" (right), proving that Northern Wei had Left and Right Scholar Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: says Shan Wei "later was regularized as lang of the famous scholars"; ming (famous) must corrupt zuo (left) or you (right), proving Northern Wei had left and right scholar langzhong.

sentences.zh: 至於「左、右司郎中」，當時並無此官。

translations.literal: As for "Left and Right Bureau Langzhong," at that time there was no such office.
translations.idiomatic: As for "left and right bureau langzhong," no such office existed then.

sentences.zh: 通典卷二僕射條附有「左、右司郎中」，云：「隋煬帝三年於尚書都省初置左、右司郎二人」，此即隋書卷二八百官志下煬帝所置之「都司郎」。

translations.literal: Tongdian juan 2, entry on Vice Directors, appends "Left and Right Bureau Langzhong," saying: "In the third year of Emperor Yang of Sui, at the Masters of Writing headquarters two Left and Right Bureau Lang were first established"—these are the "Directors of the Headquarters" placed by Emperor Yang in Sui shu juan 28, Monograph on the Hundred Offices, lower.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian juan 2 (vice directors) appends "left and right bureau langzhong," noting that in Sui Yangdi year 3 two such officers were first set at the Masters of Writing headquarters—the "directors of the headquarters" of Sui shu juan 28 (offices monograph, lower).

sentences.zh: 隋於諸曹郎中都去「中」字，故此官初置也只稱左、右司郎，直至唐代始名「左、右司郎中」。

translations.literal: Sui dropped the character "zhong" (central) from all bureau lang offices; hence when this office was first created it was called only Left and Right Bureau Lang—not until the Tang was it named "Left and Right Bureau Langzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Sui dropped zhong (central) from bureau lang titles; the post began as left and right bureau lang and only in Tang became "left and right bureau langzhong."

sentences.zh: 隋前不聞有此官。

translations.literal: Before Sui this office was not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing of the sort is attested before Sui.

sentences.zh: 這裏原文當也是「左士郎中」，與墓誌同，後人以「左士」之名罕見，妄改作「左司郎中」。

translations.literal: The original text here should also have been "Left Scholar Langzhong," the same as the epitaph; later men, because the name "Left Scholar" was rare, rashly changed it to "Left Bureau Langzhong."
translations.idiomatic: The original here should read "left scholar langzhong," as on the epitaph; later editors, finding "left scholar" unfamiliar, rashly wrote "left bureau langzhong."

sentences.zh: 正始四年薨 墓誌集釋元思墓誌

translations.literal: Died in the fourth year of Zhengshi. Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Si
translations.idiomatic: "Died in Zhengshi year 4": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Si

translations.literal: 〈plate 155〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 155

sentences.zh: 「四年」作「三年」。

translations.literal: Has "fourth year" written as "third year."
translations.idiomatic: reads "fourth year" as "third year."

sentences.zh: 疑傳誤。

translations.literal: The biography is probably in error.
translations.idiomatic: The life is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 除持節冠軍將軍幽州刺史 按墓誌集釋元彥

translations.literal: Appointed Bearer of the Staff, Champion General, and Inspector of You Province. Commentary: Muzhi jishi, Yuan Yan
translations.idiomatic: "Appointed bearer of the staff, champion general, and inspector of You": Muzhi jishi, Yuan Yan

translations.idiomatic: Jinglue

translations.idiomatic: plate 156

sentences.zh: 稱：「延昌之末，遷為持節都督豳州諸軍事、豳州刺史。

translations.literal: It states: "At the end of Yanchang he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Bing Province armies, and Inspector of Bing Province."
translations.idiomatic: states: "At the end of Yanchang he was made bearer of the staff, commander of Bing armies, and inspector of Bing."

sentences.zh: 」下云「剋莅西蕃」，與豳州地望相合。

translations.literal: " Below it says "he took up the western frontier," which matches Bing's geography.
translations.idiomatic: " Below, "he took up the western frontier" fits Bing's geography.

sentences.zh: 這裏「幽」字當是「豳」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "You" must be a corruption of "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: Here You must corrupt Bing.

sentences.zh: 改服錫衰 諸本「錫」作「裼」，北史百衲本作「錫」。

translations.literal: Changed mourning to fine hemp. In various editions "xi" (fine hemp) is written as "ti" (exposed); the Beishi Bai nang edition has "xi."
translations.idiomatic: "Changed mourning to fine hemp": editions read xi (fine hemp) as ti (exposed); Beishi Bai nang has xi.

sentences.zh: 按「錫衰」見禮記喪服小記。

translations.literal: Commentary: "Fine hemp mourning" appears in the Liji, "Mourning Garments," minor record.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "fine hemp mourning" appears in Liji, "Mourning Garments," minor record.

sentences.zh: 「錫」是細布。

translations.literal: "Xi" is fine cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Xi denotes fine cloth.

sentences.zh: 「裼」乃「錫」之形訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Ti" is a graphic corruption of "xi"; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Ti is a graphic corruption of xi; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 後復本封尒朱榮之入洛超避難洛南遇寇見害 按卷一０莊帝紀武泰元年四月庚子記河陰被殺諸王有「北平王超」，是月甲辰記「以北平王超還復為安定王」。

translations.literal: Later his original enfeoffment was restored. When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled for safety to the south of Luo and met bandits and was killed. Commentary: Juan 10, Annals of Emperor Zhuang, Wutai year 1, fourth month, day gengzi, records those princes killed at Heyin, including "Prince of Pingbei Chao"; that month on day jiachen it records "Prince of Pingbei Chao was restored as Prince of Anding."
translations.idiomatic: "Later his original enfeoffment was restored; when Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled south of the Luo for safety, met bandits, and was killed": Zhuangdi annals, juan 10, Wutai 1.4 gengzi, lists princes slain at Heyin, including "Prince of Pingbei Chao"; jiachen that month records "Prince of Pingbei Chao restored as Prince of Anding."

sentences.zh: 傳稱生前已復本封，疑誤。

translations.literal: The biography says he had already been restored to his original enfeoffment in life—probably an error.
translations.idiomatic: The life says he was already restored in life—probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 至於紀以超死於河陰之禍，傳稱「遇寇見害」，亦不合。

translations.literal: As for the annals saying Chao died in the Heyin calamity while the biography says "met bandits and was killed"—that too does not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The annals make Chao die at Heyin while the life says "met bandits and was killed"—another mismatch.

sentences.zh: 願平弟永平征虜將軍南州刺史 按地形志無「南州」。

translations.literal: Yuanping's younger brother Yongping, Campaign-pacifying General and Inspector of Nan Province. Commentary: The Monograph on Geography has no "Nan Province."
translations.idiomatic: "Yuanping's younger brother Yongping, campaign-pacifying general and inspector of Nan": the geography monograph has no "Nan province."

sentences.zh: 北周於今四川萬縣置南州、南都郡、源陽縣，事在後，見隋書卷二九地理志上巴東郡武寧縣條。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou placed Nan Province, Nandu commandery, and Yuanyang county at present Wan county in Sichuan—later in time—as seen in Sui shu juan 29, Monograph on Geography, upper, entry for Badong commandery, Wuning county.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Nan province, Nandu commandery, and Yuanyang county at modern Wanxian in Sichuan came later, per Sui shu juan 29 (geography, upper), Badong commandery, Wuning county.

sentences.zh: 這裏「南」下當脫一字。

translations.literal: Here below "Nan" one character must have dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: Here one character must have dropped after "Nan."
